title.raw: 卷八十二 列傳第七十: 儒林下 Volume 82 Biographies 70: Confucian Scholars 2

sentences.zh: 儒林下

translations.literal: Confucian Scholars, Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian Scholars, Part Two

sentences.zh: 列傳第七十儒林下

translations.literal: Biography 70: Confucian Scholars, Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 70: Confucian Scholars, Part Two

sentences.zh: 沈重樊深熊安生樂遜黎景熙冀俊趙文深辛彥之何妥蕭該包愷房暉遠馬光劉焯劉炫褚暉顧彪魯世達張沖王孝籍

translations.literal: Shen Chong, Fan Shen, Xiong Ansheng, Yue Xun, Li Jingxi, Ji Jun, Zhao Wenshen, Xin Yanzhi, He Tuo, Xiao Gai, Bao Kai, Fang Huiyuan, Ma Guang, Liu Chao, Liu Xuan, Chu Hui, Gu Biao, Lu Shida, Zhang Chong, and Wang Xiaoji.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong, Fan Shen, Xiong Ansheng, Yue Xun, Li Jingxi, Ji Jun, Zhao Wenshen, Xin Yanzhi, He Tuo, Xiao Gai, Bao Kai, Fang Huiyuan, Ma Guang, Liu Chao, Liu Xuan, Chu Hui, Gu Biao, Lu Shida, Zhang Chong, and Wang Xiaoji.

sentences.zh: 沈重，字子厚，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Chong, styled Zihou, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong, styled Zihou, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 性聰悟，弱歲而孤，居喪合禮。

translations.literal: By nature he was quick-witted; he lost his father while still young and observed mourning in accordance with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He was bright by nature, orphaned in youth, and observed mourning with proper ritual decorum.

sentences.zh: 及長，專心儒學，從師不遠千里。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he devoted himself to Confucian learning and would travel a thousand li to study under a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he devoted himself to Confucian studies, traveling great distances to seek instruction.

sentences.zh: 遂博覽群書，尤明《詩》及《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He then read widely among the classics and was especially accomplished in the Odes and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He came to read widely and was especially expert in the Book of Odes and the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝欲高置學官，以崇儒教。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang wished to elevate the academic offices in order to honor Confucian teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang wished to raise the standing of the state academies to exalt Confucian instruction.

sentences.zh: 中大通四年，乃革選，以重補國子助教。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Zhongda tong era, he reformed the selection process and appointed Chong as assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong (532), the court reformed its selections and appointed Chong assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 後除《五經》博士。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Erudite of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Erudite of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝之在籓也，甚歎異之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was still in his princely fief, he greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was still a prince, he held Chong in exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 及即位，乃遣主書何武迎重西上。

translations.literal: When Yuan took the throne, he sent the chief clerk He Wu west to escort Chong to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his accession, Yuan sent Chief Clerk He Wu west to bring Chong to court.

sentences.zh: 魏平江陵，重乃留事梁主蕭察，累遷都官尚書，領羽林監。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, Chong remained to serve the Liang ruler Xiao Cha, rising through repeated promotions to Minister of the Court for State Ceremonies and concurrently Superintendent of the Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei captured Jiangling, Chong remained in the service of the Liang ruler Xiao Cha, rising to Minister of the Court for State Ceremonies while also holding the post of Superintendent of the Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 察又令重于合歡殿講《周禮》。

translations.literal: Cha also had Chong lecture on the Rites of Zhou in the Hall of Joined Delight.
translations.idiomatic: Cha also had him expound the Rites of Zhou in the Hall of Joined Delight.

sentences.zh: 武帝以重經明行修，乃遣宣納上士柳裘致書禮聘，又敕襄州總管衛公直敦喻遣之，在途供給，務從優厚。

translations.literal: Because Chong was accomplished in the classics and cultivated in conduct, Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou sent the Senior Adviser Liu Qiu with a letter of ceremonial invitation; he also ordered the regional commander of Xiangzhou, Duke Wei of Wei, to urge him onward with repeated instructions, and supplies on the road were to be as generous as possible.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Chong was learned in the classics and upright in conduct, Emperor Wu of Zhou sent Senior Adviser Liu Qiu with a formal letter of invitation and ordered Xiangzhou’s regional commander, Duke Wei, to press him to come; his travel provisions were to be as generous as possible.

sentences.zh: 保定末，至於京師，詔令討論《五經》，並校定鐘律。

translations.literal: At the end of the Baoding era he reached the capital, and an edict ordered him to discuss the Five Classics and to collate and fix the pitch-pipes and musical standards.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Baoding era he reached the capital, where an edict charged him to deliberate on the Five Classics and to collate the pitch-pipes and musical standards.

sentences.zh: 天和中，復於紫極殿講三教義，朝士、儒生、桑門、道士至者二千餘人。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he again lectured on the meaning of the Three Teachings in the Hall of Purple Perfection; more than two thousand court officials, Confucian scholars, Buddhist monks, and Daoist priests attended.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era he again expounded the Three Teachings in the Hall of Purple Perfection before an audience of more than two thousand court officials, Confucian scholars, Buddhist monks, and Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 重辭義優洽，樞機明辯，凡所解釋，咸為諸儒所推。

translations.literal: Chong’s exposition was fluent and thorough, his reasoning clear and incisive, and whatever he explained was praised by the Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Chong’s exposition was fluent and thorough, his reasoning sharp and incisive, and every explanation he gave won the acclaim of the assembled scholars.

sentences.zh: 六年，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、露門博士，仍于露門館為皇太子講《論語》。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Director with the same powers as the Three Dukes, and Erudite of the Lumen Gate, and he continued to lecture on the Analects to the crown prince at the Lumen Gate Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made General of Agile Cavalry, Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes, and Erudite of the Lumen Gate, and he continued to lecture on the Analects to the crown prince at the Lumen Gate Academy.

sentences.zh: 建德末，表請還梁，武帝優詔不許。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiande era he memorialized requesting to return to Liang; the emperor issued a gracious edict refusing permission.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiande era he submitted a memorial asking to return to Liang; the emperor replied with a gracious edict refusing permission.

sentences.zh: 重固請，乃許。

translations.literal: Chong pressed his request firmly, and only then was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chong pressed his request again, and at last permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 為遣小司門上士楊汪送之。

translations.literal: The court sent the Junior Keeper of the Inner Gate, Senior Gentleman Yang Wang, to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Junior Keeper of the Inner Gate, Senior Gentleman Yang Wang, to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 梁主蕭巋拜重散騎常侍、太常卿。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler Xiao Kui appointed Chong Palace Attendant at Large and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler Xiao Kui appointed him Palace Attendant at Large and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，來朝京師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang he came to court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daxiang (581) he came to the capital on a court visit.

sentences.zh: 開皇三年卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Kaihuang, at the age of eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Kaihuang (583), aged eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝遣舍人蕭子寶祭以少牢，贈使持節、上開府儀同三司、許州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui sent the palace attendant Xiao Zibao to offer the secondary sacrifice, and posthumously conferred on him the title of Commissioner with extraordinary powers, Director with the same powers as the Three Dukes of the first rank, and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui sent Palace Attendant Xiao Zibao to offer the secondary sacrifice and posthumously conferred on him the title of Commissioner with Extraordinary Powers, First-Rank Director with Powers Equal to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 重學業該博，為當世儒宗。

translations.literal: Chong’s learning was comprehensive and broad, and he was the leading Confucian authority of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Chong’s scholarship was comprehensive, and he was regarded as the leading Confucian authority of his age.

sentences.zh: 至於陰陽圖緯、道經、釋典，無不通涉。

translations.literal: As for yin-yang lore, apocryphal texts, Daoist scriptures, and Buddhist sutras, there was none he did not study.
translations.idiomatic: He also ranged across yin-yang lore, apocryphal texts, Daoist scriptures, and Buddhist sutras without exception.

sentences.zh: 著《周禮義》三十一卷、《儀禮義》三十五卷、《禮記義》三十卷、《毛詩義》二十八卷、《喪服經義》五卷、《周禮音》一卷、《儀禮音》一卷、《禮記音》二卷、《毛詩音》二卷。

translations.literal: He authored thirty-one juan of Exegesis on the Rites of Zhou, thirty-five juan of Exegesis on the Ceremonies, thirty juan of Exegesis on the Record of Rites, twenty-eight juan of Exegesis on the Mao Odes, five juan of Exegesis on the Canon of Mourning Garments, and one juan each of phonological studies on the Rites of Zhou and the Ceremonies, two juan on the Record of Rites, and two juan on the Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Exegesis on the Rites of Zhou in thirty-one juan, Exegesis on the Ceremonies in thirty-five juan, Exegesis on the Record of Rites in thirty juan, Exegesis on the Mao Odes in twenty-eight juan, Exegesis on the Canon of Mourning Garments in five juan, and phonological studies on the Rites of Zhou, the Ceremonies, the Record of Rites, and the Mao Odes.

sentences.zh: 樊深，字文深，河樂猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Fan Shen, styled Wenshen, was a native of Yishi in Hele.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shen, styled Wenshen, was a native of Yishi in Hele.

sentences.zh: 事繼母甚謹，弱冠好學，負書從師於河西，講習《五經》，晝夜不倦。

translations.literal: He served his stepmother with great reverence; in his youth he loved learning, shouldered his books, and followed teachers in Hexi, studying the Five Classics day and night without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He served his stepmother with great devotion; in his youth he loved learning, shouldered his books, and followed teachers in Hexi, studying the Five Classics day and night without fatigue.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，隨軍征討，以功累遷中散大夫。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era of Wei he followed the army on campaign and, for merit, was repeatedly promoted to Palace Gentleman for Regular Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongan era of Wei he campaigned with the army and, for his achievements, rose repeatedly to Palace Gentleman for Regular Attendance.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀書，見吾丘子，遂歸侍養。

translations.literal: Once while reading he came upon the story of Wuqiu Zi and returned home to attend to his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while reading, he came upon the story of Wuqiu Zi and returned home to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，樊王二姓舉義，為魏所誅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, the Fan and Wang clans raised troops in righteousness and were executed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved the capital west, the Fan and Wang clans rose in loyal protest and were put to death by Wei.

sentences.zh: 深父保周、叔父歡周並被害。

translations.literal: Shen’s father Bao Zhou and his uncle Huan Zhou were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen’s father Bao Zhou and his uncle Huan Zhou were both killed in the purge.

sentences.zh: 深因避難，墜崖傷足，絕食再宿。

translations.literal: Shen fled to escape disaster, fell from a cliff and injured his foot, and went without food for two nights.
translations.idiomatic: Shen fled the slaughter, fell from a cliff and injured his foot, and went without food for two nights.

sentences.zh: 於後遇得一簞餅，欲食之，然念繼母老痺，或免虜掠，乃弗食。

translations.literal: Later he found a basket of cakes and wished to eat, but thinking that his stepmother was old and crippled and might be spared capture by the enemy, he did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he found a basket of cakes and was about to eat, but remembering that his aged and crippled stepmother might yet escape capture, he refused to touch them.

sentences.zh: 夜中匍匐尋覓，母得見，因以饋母。

translations.literal: At night he crawled on hands and knees searching for her; when he found his mother, he gave the food to her.
translations.idiomatic: That night he crawled about searching for her; when he found his mother, he gave her the cakes.

sentences.zh: 還復遁去，改易姓名，遊學于汾晉間。

translations.literal: He then fled again, changed his name, and traveled to study in the Fen and Jin regions.
translations.idiomatic: He fled again, changed his name, and traveled to study in the Fen and Jin regions.

sentences.zh: 習天文及算曆之術。

translations.literal: He studied astronomy and the arts of calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He also studied astronomy and calendrical computation.

sentences.zh: 後為人所告，囚送河東。

translations.literal: Later someone reported him, and he was imprisoned and sent to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone denounced him, and he was imprisoned and sent to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 屬東魏將韓軌長史張曜重其儒學，延深至家，因是便得逃隱。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yao, chief clerk to the Eastern Wei general Han Gui, valued his Confucian learning and invited Shen to his home, whereby he was able to escape and go into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yao, chief clerk to the Eastern Wei general Han Gui, valued his scholarship and took him into his household, allowing him to escape and live in hiding.

sentences.zh: 周文平河東，贈保周南郢州刺史，歡周儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou pacified Hedong, he posthumously conferred on Bao Zhou the title of Governor of Nan’e and on Huan Zhou Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou pacified Hedong, he posthumously made Bao Zhou Governor of Nan’e and Huan Zhou a Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 深歸葬其父，負土成墳。

translations.literal: Shen returned to bury his father and carried earth on his back to build the tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: Shen returned to bury his father and carried earth on his back to build the tomb mound himself.

sentences.zh: 尋而於謹引為府參軍事，令在館授教子孫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yu Jin recommended him as a staff officer in his headquarters and had him teach the sons and grandsons in the residence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yu Jin took him on as a staff officer and had him teach the sons and grandsons in his household.

sentences.zh: 周文置學東館，教諸將子弟，以深為博士。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou established a school in the Eastern Hall to instruct the sons of the generals, appointing Shen as erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou established a school in the Eastern Hall to educate the sons of his generals and appointed Shen its erudite.

sentences.zh: 深經學通贍，每解書，多引漢魏以來諸家義而說之。

translations.literal: Shen was thoroughly versed in the classics, and whenever he expounded a text he would cite the interpretations of various schools from Han and Wei times.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was thoroughly versed in the classics; whenever he lectured, he drew on interpretations from Han and Wei scholars of many schools.

sentences.zh: 故後生聽其言者，不能曉悟，背而譏之曰：「樊生講書，多門戶，不可解。

translations.literal: Therefore the younger students who heard him could not understand him clearly, and behind his back they mocked him, saying, “When Master Fan lectures, there are too many schools of interpretation—it cannot be understood.”
translations.idiomatic: His younger listeners often could not follow him and mocked him behind his back: “When Master Fan lectures, there are too many schools at once—nothing can be made of it.”

sentences.zh: 」然儒者推其博物。

translations.literal: Yet the Confucian scholars admired his encyclopedic learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the scholarly community still admired his encyclopedic learning.

sentences.zh: 性好學，老而不怠。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning and never slackened even in old age.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved learning and never slackened, even in old age.

sentences.zh: 朝暮還往，常據鞍讀書，至馬驚墜地，損折支體，終亦不改。

translations.literal: Going to and from court morning and evening, he would often read in the saddle; when his horse bolted and threw him, breaking his limbs, he still did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening on the road to court he would read in the saddle; when his horse bolted and threw him, breaking his limbs, he still did not change the habit.

sentences.zh: 後除國子博士，賜姓萬紐於氏。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Erudite of the National University and granted the surname Wanniu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Erudite of the National University and granted the surname Wanniu.

sentences.zh: 天平二年，遷縣伯中大夫，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianping he was promoted to Grand Master of the State with the rank of district marquis and additionally made Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianping he was promoted to Grand Master of the State with the rank of district marquis and given additional powers equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 建德元年，表乞骸骨，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiande he submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiande he asked to retire on grounds of age, and the court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有疑議，常召問焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had doubtful matters, he was regularly summoned for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court faced doubtful matters, he was regularly summoned for consultation.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 深既專經，又讀諸史及《倉》、《雅》、篆、籀、陰陽、卜筮之書。

translations.literal: Shen devoted himself to the classics and also read the various histories, the Cang Jie primer, the Erya, seal and clerical scripts, and books on yin-yang and divination.
translations.idiomatic: Shen devoted himself to the classics and also read histories, primers such as the Cang Jie and Erya, seal and clerical scripts, and works on yin-yang lore and divination.

sentences.zh: 學雖博贍，訥於辭辯，故不為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Although his learning was broad and ample, he was slow of speech and therefore not praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Though his learning was broad, he was slow of speech and therefore won little contemporary renown.

sentences.zh: 撰《孝經》《喪服問疑》各一卷。

translations.literal: He compiled one juan each of Questions and Doubts on the Classic of Filial Piety and on Mourning Garments.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled one juan each of Questions and Doubts on the Classic of Filial Piety and on Mourning Garments.

sentences.zh: 又撰《七經異同》三卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled three juan of Differences and Agreements among the Seven Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled three juan on Differences and Agreements among the Seven Classics.

sentences.zh: 子義綱。

translations.literal: His son was Yigang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yigang.

sentences.zh: 熊安生，字植之，長樂阜城人也。

translations.literal: Xiong Ansheng, styled Zhizhi, was a native of Fucheng in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ansheng, styled Zhizhi, came from Fucheng in Changle.

sentences.zh: 少好學，勵精不倦。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and strove tirelessly without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning and strove tirelessly without slackening.

sentences.zh: 從陳達受《三傳》，從房虯受《周禮》，事徐遵明，服膺歷年，後受《禮》于李寶鼎，遂博通《五經》。

translations.literal: He studied the Three Commentaries under Chen Da, the Rites of Zhou under Fang Qiu, and served Xu Zunming for many years with devoted respect; later he received instruction in the Rites from Li Baoding and thus mastered the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Three Commentaries under Chen Da, the Rites of Zhou under Fang Qiu, and studied under Xu Zunming for many years with devoted respect; later he received instruction in the Rites from Li Baoding and came to master the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 然專以《三禮》教授，弟子自遠方至者千餘人。

translations.literal: Yet he specialized in teaching the Three Rites, and more than a thousand disciples came from distant places.
translations.idiomatic: He specialized in teaching the Three Rites, and more than a thousand disciples came from distant places to study with him.

sentences.zh: 乃討論圖緯，捃摭異聞。

translations.literal: He then investigated apocryphal texts and gathered unusual lore.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated apocryphal texts and gathered unusual traditions.

sentences.zh: 先儒所未悟者，皆發明之。

translations.literal: Whatever earlier scholars had not yet understood, he elucidated.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever earlier scholars had not yet understood, he elucidated.

sentences.zh: 齊河清中，陽休之特奏為國子博士。

translations.literal: In the Heqing era of Northern Qi, Yang Xiuzhi specially memorialized that he be appointed Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the Heqing era of Northern Qi, Yang Xiuzhi specially memorialized that he be appointed Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 時西朝既行《周禮》，公卿以下，多習其業，有宿疑碩滯者數十條，皆莫能詳辨。

translations.literal: At that time the Western court had already adopted the Rites of Zhou; among dukes, ministers, and those below, many studied this subject, yet several dozen longstanding doubts and knotty points remained that none could clearly resolve.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Western court had adopted the Rites of Zhou; among dukes, ministers, and officials below, many studied the text, yet several dozen longstanding doubts remained that no one could clearly resolve.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，周齊通好，兵部尹公正使焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, when Zhou and Qi were on friendly terms, Yin Gongzheng of the Ministry of War was sent as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe (568), when Zhou and Qi were on friendly terms, Yin Gongzheng of the Ministry of War was sent as envoy.

sentences.zh: 與齊人語及《周禮》，齊人不能對。

translations.literal: When he spoke with the men of Qi about the Rites of Zhou, the men of Qi could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke with the men of Qi about the Rites of Zhou, they could not answer.

sentences.zh: 乃令安生至賓館，與公正言。

translations.literal: They then had Ansheng come to the guest quarters to speak with Gongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: They then had Ansheng come to the guest quarters to debate with Gongzheng.

sentences.zh: 公正有口辯，安生語所未至者，便撮機要而驟問之。

translations.literal: Gongzheng was skilled in debate; wherever Ansheng’s exposition had not yet reached, he would seize the crucial point and press him with sudden questions.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzheng was skilled in debate; wherever Ansheng’s exposition had not yet reached, he would seize the crucial point and press him with sudden questions.

sentences.zh: 安生曰：「《禮》義弘深，自有條貫，必欲升堂睹奧，寧可汨其先後？

translations.literal: Ansheng said, “The meaning of the Rites is vast and deep and has its own systematic order; if you wish to ascend the hall and glimpse the inner sanctum, how can you muddy the sequence by jumping ahead?”
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng said, “The meaning of the Rites is vast and deep and follows its own order; if you wish to ascend the hall and glimpse the inner sanctum, how can you muddy the sequence by leaping ahead?”

sentences.zh: 但能留意，當為次第陳之。

translations.literal: “If you will pay attention, I shall set them forth for you in due order.”
translations.idiomatic: “If you will pay attention, I shall set them forth for you in due order.”

sentences.zh: 」公正於是問所疑，安生皆為一一演說，咸究其根本。

translations.literal: Gongzheng then asked his doubts, and Ansheng explained each one, tracing every point to its root.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzheng then asked his doubts, and Ansheng explained each one, tracing every point to its root.

sentences.zh: 公正嗟服。

translations.literal: Gongzheng sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzheng sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 還，具言之于武帝，帝大欽重之。

translations.literal: On his return he reported fully to the emperor, who greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported fully to the emperor, who held Ansheng in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 及入鄴，安生遽令掃門。

translations.literal: When they entered Ye, Ansheng immediately ordered the gate swept.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army entered Ye, Ansheng immediately ordered his gate swept.

sentences.zh: 家人怪而問之，安生曰：「周帝重道尊儒，必將見我矣。

translations.literal: His family wondered and asked him; Ansheng said, “The Zhou emperor honors the Way and esteems Confucian learning—he is sure to visit me.”
translations.idiomatic: His family wondered and asked why; Ansheng said, “The Zhou emperor honors the Way and esteems Confucian learning—he is sure to visit me.”

sentences.zh: 」俄而帝幸其第，詔不聽拜，親執其手，引與同坐，謂曰：「朕未能去兵，以此為愧。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor visited his residence, ordered that he need not bow, personally took his hand, and seated him beside himself, saying, “I have not yet been able to lay down arms—this shames me.”
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor visited his home, ordered that he need not bow, personally took his hand, and seated him beside himself, saying, “I have not yet been able to lay down arms—for this I am ashamed.”

sentences.zh: 」安生曰：「黃帝尚有阪泉之戰，況陛下龔行天罰乎！

translations.literal: Ansheng said, “Even the Yellow Emperor still had the battle at Banquan—how much more so when Your Majesty is carrying out Heaven’s punishment!”
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng said, “Even the Yellow Emperor still fought at Banquan—how much more when Your Majesty is carrying out Heaven’s punishment!”

sentences.zh: 」帝又曰：「齊氏賦役繁興，竭人財力，朕救焚拯溺，思革其弊，欲以府庫及三台雜物散之百姓，公以為何如？

translations.literal: The emperor also said, “Under the Qi, taxes and corvée were heavy and exhausted the people’s wealth and strength; I am rescuing them from fire and flood and wish to reform these abuses. I intend to distribute the contents of the treasuries and the miscellaneous goods of the Three Platforms among the common people—what do you think?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said, “Under the Qi, taxes and corvée were heavy and drained the people’s wealth; I am rescuing them from fire and flood and wish to reform these abuses. I intend to distribute the contents of the treasuries and the miscellaneous goods of the Three Platforms among the people—what do you think?”

sentences.zh: 」安生曰：「昔武王克商，散鹿台之財，發巨橋之粟，陛下此詔，異代同美。

translations.literal: Ansheng said, “When King Wu overcame Shang, he dispersed the wealth of Lutai and released the grain of Juqiao; Your Majesty’s edict matches the beauty of that ancient example.”
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng said, “When King Wu overcame Shang, he dispersed the wealth of Lutai and released the grain of Juqiao; Your Majesty’s edict matches the beauty of that ancient deed.”

sentences.zh: 」帝又曰：「朕何如武王？

translations.literal: The emperor also asked, “How do I compare with King Wu?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also asked, “How do I compare with King Wu?”

sentences.zh: 」安生曰：「武王伐紂，懸首白旗；

translations.literal: Ansheng said, “King Wu attacked Zhou and hung his head on a white flag;”
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng said, “King Wu attacked Zhou and hung his head on a white flag;”

sentences.zh: 陛下平齊，兵不血刃，愚謂聖略為優。

translations.literal: “Your Majesty pacified Qi without bloodshed on the blades—in my humble view your sagely strategy is superior.”
translations.idiomatic: “Your Majesty pacified Qi without bloodshed on the blades—in my humble view your sagely strategy is superior.”

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅，賜帛三百匹、米三百石、宅一區，並賜象笏及九鐶金帶，自餘什物稱是。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk, three hundred shi of grain, and one residence, and also granted an ivory tablet and a gold belt with nine rings; the remaining goods were commensurate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk, three hundred shi of grain, and a residence, along with an ivory court tablet and a gold belt with nine rings; the remaining gifts were of like generosity.

sentences.zh: 又詔所司給安車駟馬，令隨駕入朝，並敕所在供給。

translations.literal: He also ordered the relevant offices to supply a four-horse carriage and commanded him to enter court with the imperial procession, with orders that local authorities provide for him along the way.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the relevant offices to supply a four-horse carriage and commanded him to enter court with the imperial procession, with orders that local authorities provide for him along the way.

sentences.zh: 至京，敕令於大乘佛寺，參議五禮。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, an edict ordered him to take part at the Mahayana Monastery in deliberating on the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital, an edict ordered him to take part at the Mahayana Monastery in deliberating on the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，拜露門博士、下大夫，時年八十餘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was appointed Erudite of the Lumen Gate and Junior Grand Master; he was then more than eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was appointed Erudite of the Lumen Gate and Junior Grand Master, being then more than eighty years old.

sentences.zh: 尋致仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he retired and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he retired from office and died at home.

sentences.zh: 安生既學為儒宗，嘗受其業，擅名於後者，有馬榮伯、張黑奴、竇士榮、孔籠、劉焯、劉炫等，皆其門人焉。

translations.literal: Ansheng, as the leading Confucian authority of his age, had among those who studied under him and won later fame Ma Rongbo, Zhang Heinu, Dou Shirong, Kong Long, Liu Chao, Liu Xuan, and others—all were his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: As the leading Confucian authority of his age, Ansheng had among his disciples those who later won fame, including Ma Rongbo, Zhang Heinu, Dou Shirong, Kong Long, Liu Chao, and Liu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 所撰《周禮義疏》二十卷，《禮記義疏》三十卷、《孝經義》一卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He authored twenty juan of Exegesis and Commentary on the Rites of Zhou, thirty juan of Exegesis and Commentary on the Record of Rites, and one juan of Exegesis on the Classic of Filial Piety, all of which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included twenty juan of Exegesis and Commentary on the Rites of Zhou, thirty juan on the Record of Rites, and one juan of Exegesis on the Classic of Filial Piety, all of which circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 安生與同郡宗道暉、張暉、紀顯敬、徐遵明等為祖師。

translations.literal: Ansheng, together with his fellow townsman Zong Daohui, Zhang Hui, Ji Xianjing, and Xu Zunming, were regarded as founding masters.
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng, together with his fellow townsman Zong Daohui, Zhang Hui, Ji Xianjing, and Xu Zunming, were regarded as founding masters of the school.

sentences.zh: 道暉好著高翅帽、大屐，州將初臨，輒服以謁見，仰頭舉肘，拜於屐上，自言學士比三公。

translations.literal: Daohui liked to wear a high-winged cap and large clogs; whenever a regional commander first arrived, he would dress thus to pay his respects, lifting his head and elbows to bow atop his clogs, declaring that a scholar was the equal of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Daohui liked to wear a high-winged cap and large clogs; whenever a regional commander first arrived, he would dress thus to pay his respects, lifting his head and elbows to bow atop his clogs while declaring that a scholar was the equal of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 後齊任城王湝鞭之，道暉徐呼安偉，安偉出，謂人曰：「我受鞭，不漢體。

translations.literal: Later the Prince of Rencheng of Qi, Xiao Kan, whipped him; Daohui slowly called for An Wei, and when An Wei came out he said to the onlookers, “I received the lash, but I am not of Han dress.”
translations.idiomatic: Later the Prince of Rencheng of Qi, Xiao Kan, whipped him; Daohui slowly called for An Wei, and when An Wei emerged he told the onlookers, “I took the lash, but I am not dressed as a Han man.”

sentences.zh: 」復躡屐而去。

translations.literal: He then strode off again in his clogs.
translations.idiomatic: He then strode off again in his clogs.

sentences.zh: 冀州人為之語曰「顯公鐘，宋公鼓，宗道暉屐，李洛姬肚」，謂之四大。

translations.literal: The people of Jizhou made a saying of it: “Abbot Xian’s bell, Lord Song’s drum, Zong Daohui’s clogs, and Li Luoji’s belly”—these were called the Four Great Ones.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jizhou made a saying of it: “Abbot Xian’s bell, Lord Song’s drum, Zong Daohui’s clogs, and Li Luoji’s belly”—these were called the Four Wonders.

sentences.zh: 顯公，沙門也，宋公，安德太守也；

translations.literal: Xian Gong was a Buddhist monk; Lord Song was the Administrator of Ande;
translations.idiomatic: “Abbot Xian” was a Buddhist monk; “Lord Song” was the Administrator of Ande;

sentences.zh: 洛姬，婦人也。

translations.literal: Luoji was a woman.
translations.idiomatic: Luoji was a woman.

sentences.zh: 安生在山東時，歲歲遊講，從之者傾郡縣。

translations.literal: When Ansheng was in Shandong, every year he traveled about lecturing, and those who followed him filled commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: While Ansheng was in Shandong, he lectured on tour every year, and followers thronged from every commandery and county.

sentences.zh: 或誑之曰：「某村古鹆塚，是晉河南將軍熊光，去七十二世。

translations.literal: Someone deceived him, saying, "In such-and-such a village is an ancient magpie grave mound—it is Xiong Guang, Jin General of Henan, seventy-two generations removed."
translations.idiomatic: Someone tricked him, saying, "In a certain village is an ancient magpie grave mound belonging to Xiong Guang, Jin General of Henan, seventy-two generations back."

sentences.zh: 舊有碑，為村人埋匿。

translations.literal: There was formerly a stele, which the villagers had buried and hidden.
translations.idiomatic: An old stele had been buried and hidden by the villagers.

sentences.zh: 」安生掘地求之，不得，連年訟焉。

translations.literal: " Ansheng dug in the earth seeking it but did not find it, and for years he brought lawsuits over the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng dug in the earth seeking it but found nothing, and for years he kept bringing lawsuits over the matter.

sentences.zh: 冀州長史鄭大訁雚判之曰：「七十二世，乃是羲皇上人；

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk of Jizhou, Zheng Dahuan, judged the case, saying, "Seventy-two generations—that would be a man of Fuxi the August One's age;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Dahuan, chief clerk of Jizhou, ruled on the case: "Seventy-two generations—that would be a man of Fuxi the August One's age;

sentences.zh: 河南將軍，晉無此號。

translations.literal: General of Henan—Jin had no such title.
translations.idiomatic: General of Henan—there was no such title in Jin.

sentences.zh: 訴非理記。

translations.literal: The suit is an unreasonable record."
translations.idiomatic: This suit has no basis in reason."

sentences.zh: 」安生率其族向鹆塚而號。

translations.literal: " Ansheng led his clan toward the magpie grave mound and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng led his clan to the magpie grave mound and wailed aloud.

sentences.zh: 將通名，見徐之才、和士開二人相對，以徐之才諱「雄」，和士開諱「安」，乃稱「觸觸生」，群公哂之。

translations.literal: When he was about to give his name, he saw Xu Zhicai and He Shikai facing each other; since Xu Zhicai tabooed the character "xiong" and He Shikai tabooed "an," he called himself "Mr. Chuchu"—the assembled lords sneered at him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to announce his name, he saw Xu Zhicai and He Shikai facing each other; because Xu Zhicai avoided the character xiong and He Shikai avoided an, he called himself "Mr. Chuchu"—and the assembled lords laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 樂遜，字遵賢，河東猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Yue Xun, styled Zunxian, was a native of Yishi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Xun, whose courtesy name was Zunxian, came from Yishi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼有成人之操，從徐遵明于趙、魏間，受《孝經》、《喪服》、《論語》、《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《易》、《左氏春秋》大義。

translations.literal: In youth he had the conduct of a grown man; he followed Xu Zunming in the Zhao and Wei region and received the essential meanings of the Classic of Filial Piety, Mourning Garments, the Analects, the Odes, the Documents, the Rites, the Changes, and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he already showed mature conduct; he studied under Xu Zunming in Zhao and Wei and mastered the essential meanings of the Classic of Filial Piety, Mourning Garments, the Analects, the Odes, the Documents, the Rites, the Changes, and the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 尋而山東寇亂，學者散逸，遜於擾擾之中，猶志道不倦。

translations.literal: Before long bandits ravaged Shandong and scholars scattered; amid the turmoil, Xun yet pursued the Way without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long bandits ravaged Shandong and scholars scattered; amid the turmoil Xun still pursued the Way without tiring.

sentences.zh: 大統七年，除子都督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong he was made Junior Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Datong era he was made junior commandant.

sentences.zh: 九年，太尉李弼請遜教授諸子。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Grand Commandant Li Bi requested that Xun instruct his sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Grand Commandant Li Bi asked Xun to instruct his sons.

sentences.zh: 既而周文盛選賢良，授以守令。

translations.literal: Before long Duke Wen of Zhou extensively selected the worthy and good and appointed them as prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Duke Wen of Zhou conducted a broad selection of worthy men and appointed them prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 相府戶曹柳敏、行台郎中盧光、河東郡丞辛粲相繼舉遜，稱有牧人之才。

translations.literal: The Household Clerk Liu Min of the chancellor's office, the Secretariat Gentleman of the traveling secretariat Lu Guang, and the Assistant Commandery Administrator Xin Can of Hedong in succession recommended Xun, declaring that he possessed the talent to govern the people.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min, household clerk of the chancellor's office, Lu Guang, secretariat gentleman of the traveling secretariat, and Xin Can, assistant administrator of Hedong, recommended Xun in turn, praising his talent for governing the people.

sentences.zh: 弼請留不遣。

translations.literal: Bi requested that he be retained and not sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi asked that he be kept and not sent away.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，周文召遜教授諸子。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, Duke Wen of Zhou summoned Xun to instruct his sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, Duke Wen of Zhou summoned Xun to teach his sons.

sentences.zh: 在館六年，與諸儒分授經業，講《孝經》、《論語》、《毛詩》及服虔所注《春秋左氏傳》。

translations.literal: He remained at the academy six years, dividing the teaching of the classics with the various Confucians, lecturing on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao Odes, and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn as annotated by Fu Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He spent six years at the academy, sharing classical instruction with other Confucian masters, and lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao Odes, and Fu Qian's commentary on the Zuo version of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝踐阼，以遜有理務材，除秋官府上士，轉小師氏下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, since Xun had talent for practical administration, he was made Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Punishments and then transferred to Lower Grand Master of the Junior Master Shi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Xun was made senior clerk of the Ministry of Punishments and then lower grand master of the Junior Master Shi, on account of his talent for practical administration.

sentences.zh: 自譙王儉以下，並束脩行弟子之禮。

translations.literal: From Prince of Qiao Jian downward, all presented the silk tribute and observed the rites due a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: From Prince of Qiao Jian downward, all presented silk tribute and observed the rites due a disciple.

sentences.zh: 遜以經術教授，甚有訓導之方。

translations.literal: Xun taught through the classical disciplines and possessed excellent methods of instruction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Xun taught the classics and had excellent methods of instruction and guidance.

sentences.zh: 及衛公直鎮蒲州，遜為直主簿。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei Zhi governed Puzhou, Xun became chief clerk of Zhi's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei Zhi governed Puzhou, Xun served as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 遜性柔謹，寡交遊，立身以忠信為本。

translations.literal: Xun's nature was gentle and careful; he had few social connections and grounded his conduct in loyalty and trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was gentle and cautious by nature, kept few associates, and grounded his conduct in loyalty and trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 不自矜尚。

translations.literal: He did not exalt himself.
translations.idiomatic: He never put himself forward.

sentences.zh: 每在眾言論，未嘗為人之先，學者以此稱之。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke in a gathering, he never took the lead over others; scholars for this reason praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In company he never spoke before others, and scholars praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 所著《孝經》、《論語》、《毛詩》、《左氏春秋序論》十餘篇。

translations.literal: He authored more than ten pieces including "Preface Discussions" on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao Odes, and the Zuoshi Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than ten works, including preface essays on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao Odes, and the Zuoshi Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 又著《春秋序義》，通賈、服說，發杜氏違，辭理並可觀。

translations.literal: He also authored "Preface to the Meaning of the Spring and Autumn," incorporating the explanations of Jia and Fu, exposing the errors of the Du clan; in wording and reasoning both are worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Preface to the Meaning of the Spring and Autumn, drawing on the commentaries of Jia Kui and Fu Qian while exposing flaws in Du Yu's readings—a work admirable in both style and argument.

sentences.zh: 初，周又有黎景熙，以古學顯。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Zhou there was also Li Jingxi, who became famous through ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Zhou there was also Li Jingxi, who won renown for ancient learning.

sentences.zh: 黎景熙，字季明，河間鄭人，少以孝行聞於世。

translations.literal: Li Jingxi, styled Jiming, was a man of Zheng in Hejian; from youth he was known in the world for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingxi, courtesy name Jiming, came from Zheng in Hejian and was known from youth for his filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 曾祖嶷，魏太武時，以軍功賜爵容城縣男，後為燕郡守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ni, in the time of Emperor Taiwu of Wei, was granted the title Baron of Rongcheng for military merit and later became Administrator of Yan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ni, under Emperor Taiwu of Wei, was enfeoffed as baron of Rongcheng for military merit and later served as administrator of Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖鎮、父瓊，並襲爵。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen and his father Qiong both inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen and his father Qiong both inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 季明少好讀書，性強記默識，而無應對之能。

translations.literal: Jiming from youth loved reading; he had a strong memory and silent retention but no ability in repartee.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jiming loved books; he remembered silently and retained much, but was awkward in conversation.

sentences.zh: 其從祖廣，太武時尚書郎，善古學。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Guang, in the time of Emperor Taiwu, was a Gentleman in the Masters of Writing and was skilled in ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal uncle Guang, under Emperor Taiwu, was a gentleman in the masters of writing and excelled in ancient learning.

sentences.zh: 常從吏部尚書清河崔宏受字義，又從司徒崔浩學楷篆，自是家傳其法。

translations.literal: He once received instruction in the meaning of characters from Cui Hong of Qinghe, Minister of Personnel, and also studied regular and seal script from Minister of State Cui Hao—thereafter the family transmitted this method.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the meaning of characters under Cui Hong of Qinghe, minister of personnel, and regular and seal script under Minister of State Cui Hao; the family thereafter transmitted these arts.

sentences.zh: 季明亦傳習之，頗與許氏有異。

translations.literal: Jiming also received and practiced them, differing somewhat from the Xu school.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming learned them too, though his tradition differed somewhat from the Xu school.

sentences.zh: 又好玄象，頗知術數，而落魄不事生業。

translations.literal: He also loved the arcane signs of heaven and knew something of numerology, yet he was down and out and did not pursue a livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved celestial divination and knew something of numerology, yet lived in poverty and did not pursue a regular livelihood.

sentences.zh: 有書千餘卷。

translations.literal: He had more than a thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: He owned more than a thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 雖窮居獨處，不以饑寒易操。

translations.literal: Though he dwelt in poverty alone, he did not change his principles because of hunger or cold.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lived alone in poverty, hunger and cold never changed his principles.

sentences.zh: 與范陽盧道源為莫逆交。

translations.literal: He and Lu Daoyuan of Fanyang were friends of the closest bond.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lu Daoyuan of Fanyang were the closest of friends.

sentences.zh: 永安中，道源勸令入仕，始為威烈將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era Daoyuan urged him to enter office; he first became General of Majestic Valor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongan era Daoyuan urged him into office; he first became general of majestic valor.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，季明乃寓居伊洛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Jiming then took up residence in the Yi and Luo region.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Jiming settled in the Yi and Luo region.

sentences.zh: 侯景徇地河外，召季明從軍，稍遷黎陽郡守。

translations.literal: Hou Jing overran the lands beyond the Yellow River and summoned Jiming to join his army; he was soon promoted to Administrator of Liyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing overran the lands beyond the Yellow River, summoned Jiming to his army, and soon made him administrator of Liyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 季明從至懸瓠，察景終不足恃，遂去之。

translations.literal: Jiming followed him as far as Xuanhu, perceived that Jing in the end could not be relied upon, and left him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming followed him to Xuanhu, saw that Hou Jing could not be relied upon in the end, and left him.

sentences.zh: 客於潁川。

translations.literal: He lodged as a guest in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed in Yingchuan as a guest.

sentences.zh: 時王思政鎮潁川，累使召季明，留於內館。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Sizheng was defending Yingchuan and repeatedly sent to summon Jiming, keeping him in the inner lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng was then defending Yingchuan, summoned Jiming repeatedly, and kept him in the inner lodge.

sentences.zh: 月餘，周文又征之，遂入關。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Duke Wen of Zhou summoned him again, and he then entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month Duke Wen of Zhou summoned him again, and he entered the passes.

sentences.zh: 乃令季明正定古今文字於東閣。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to fix and determine ancient and modern writing in the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to standardize ancient and modern writing in the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 大統末，拜著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong he was appointed Assistant Gentleman for Composition.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Datong era he was made assistant gentleman for composition.

sentences.zh: 于時倫輩，皆位兼常伯，車服華盛，唯季明獨以貧素居之，而無愧色。

translations.literal: At that time his peers all held concurrent posts as regular palace attendants, with splendid carriages and robes; only Jiming alone dwelt in poverty and simplicity, yet without a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: His peers all held concurrent posts as regular palace attendants and dressed in splendid style; only Jiming lived in poverty and simplicity without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 又勤於所職，著述不怠。

translations.literal: He was also diligent in his duties and never slackened in writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was also diligent in his duties and never slackened in his writing.

sentences.zh: 然性尤專固，不合于時，是以一為史官，遂十年不調。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was especially obstinate and inflexible, not suited to the times; therefore, once he became a historiographer, he went ten years without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stubborn by nature and ill suited to the times; once he became a historiographer, he went ten years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 武成末，遷外史下大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Wucheng he was promoted to Lower Grand Master of the Outer Historiography.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wucheng era he was promoted to lower grand master of the outer historiography.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，盛營宮室。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, palace buildings were constructed on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding palace construction was carried out on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 春夏大旱，詔公卿百僚，極言得失。

translations.literal: In spring and summer there was great drought; an edict ordered the high ministers and the hundred officials to speak to the utmost on gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and summer brought severe drought; the throne ordered ministers and officials to speak freely on what was going wrong.

sentences.zh: 季明上封事曰：

translations.literal: Jiming submitted a sealed memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jiming submitted a sealed memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞成湯遭旱，以六事自陳。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when Cheng Tang encountered drought, he confessed himself in six matters.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Cheng Tang encountered drought, he confessed his faults in six matters.

sentences.zh: 宣王太甚，而圭璧斯竭。

translations.literal: When King Xuan went too far, jade disks and bi were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When King Xuan of Zhou went too far, even jade offerings were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 豈非遠慮元元，俯哀黎庶。

translations.literal: Was this not because he looked far to the common people and bowed in pity to the masses?
translations.idiomatic: Surely that was because he looked to the welfare of the people and pitied the masses.

sentences.zh: 今農要之月，時雨猶愆，率土之心，有懷渴仰。

translations.literal: Now in the month when agriculture is vital, timely rain is still lacking; the heart of all within the realm thirsts and looks up.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the month when agriculture matters most, timely rain is still lacking, and the whole realm looks up in thirst.

sentences.zh: 陛下垂情萬類，子愛群生，覲禮百神，猶未豐洽。

translations.literal: Your Majesty extends affection to the ten thousand kinds and loves the multitude as children; you observe rites toward the hundred spirits, yet abundance is not yet full.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty cares for all living things and loves the people as his children; you perform rites to the spirits, yet blessings are not yet complete.

sentences.zh: 豈或作事不節，有違時令，舉措失中，當邀斯旱。

translations.literal: Could it be that works are not regulated, the seasons are violated, or measures are misplaced, perchance inviting this drought?
translations.idiomatic: Could it be that undertakings are ill timed, the seasons violated, or measures misplaced, and so this drought has been invited?

sentences.zh: 《春秋》，君舉必書，動為典禮。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that a ruler's every act must be written; movement is canon and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records every act of a ruler; conduct is canon and ritual.

sentences.zh: 水旱陰陽，莫不應行而至。

translations.literal: Flood, drought, yin and yang—none fail to respond to conduct and arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Flood, drought, and the balance of yin and yang all respond to how a ruler behaves.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「言行，君子之所以動天地，可不慎乎！

translations.literal: Confucius said, "Words and conduct are how the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth—can one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Words and conduct are how the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth—can one not be cautious?

sentences.zh: 」《春秋》莊公三十一年冬，不雨，《五行傳》以為是歲一年而三築台，奢侈不恤人也。

translations.literal: " The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuang year 31 winter: no rain. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year platforms were built three times in one year—extravagance without pity for the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that in the thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang of Lu, winter, there was no rain. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year three platforms were built in one year—extravagance without pity for the people.

sentences.zh: 僖公二十一年夏，大旱，《五行傳》以為時作南門，勞人興役。

translations.literal: Duke Xi year 21 summer: great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that at that time the southern gate was being built, laboring the people with corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Duke Xi of Lu, summer, there was great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that at that time the southern gate was under construction, exhausting the people with labor.

sentences.zh: 漢惠帝二年夏，大旱，五年夏，大旱，江河水少，溪澗水絕，《五行傳》以為先是發十四萬六千人城長安。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui of Han year 2 summer: great drought. Year 5 summer: great drought; the Yangtze and Yellow rivers had little water, and streams and brooks dried up. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that before this 146,000 men had been mobilized to build the walls of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Hui of Han, summer, there was great drought. In the fifth year, summer, there was great drought; the great rivers ran low and streams dried up. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that before this 146,000 men had been mobilized to build the walls of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝元狩三年夏，大旱，《五行傳》以為是歲發天下故吏，穿昆明池。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han, Yuanshou year 3 summer: great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year men throughout the realm who had formerly held office were mobilized to dig the Kunming Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanshou of Emperor Wu of Han, summer, there was great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year former officials throughout the realm were mobilized to dig the Kunming Pool.

sentences.zh: 然則土木之功，動人興役，天輒應之以異。

translations.literal: Thus works of earth and wood, moving the people with corvée—Heaven always responds with anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Thus whenever earth and wood works mobilize the people, Heaven responds with anomalies.

sentences.zh: 典籍作誡，倘或可思，上天譴告，改之則善。

translations.literal: The admonitions of the classics—perhaps they may be pondered; Heaven's reproof—if changed, then good.
translations.idiomatic: The warnings of the classics are perhaps worth pondering; Heaven's reproof, if heeded, leads to good.

sentences.zh: 今若息人省役，以答天譴，庶靈澤時降，嘉谷有時，則年登可覬，子來非晚。

translations.literal: If now the people are rested and corvée reduced, to answer Heaven's reproof, then perhaps timely blessings will descend, fine grain will ripen in season, the year's harvest may be hoped for, and the people will come as children—not late.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now rests the people and reduces corvée to answer Heaven's reproof, timely rain may fall, grain ripen, and the people come gladly—not too late.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「人亦勞止，迄可小康，惠此中國，以綏四方。

translations.literal: The Odes say, "The people also have labored; let them have a little ease; show favor to this central kingdom to bring peace to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "The people also have labored; let them have a little ease; show favor to this central kingdom to bring peace to the four quarters."

sentences.zh: 」或恐極陽生陰，秋多雨水，年復不登，人將無覬。

translations.literal: " Or perhaps one fears that when yang reaches its extreme yin is born, and in autumn there will be much rain; the year again will not yield, and the people will have nothing to hope for.
translations.idiomatic: Or perhaps when yang reaches its extreme, yin will arise; autumn may bring heavy rain, the harvest may fail again, and the people will have nothing to hope for.

sentences.zh: 如又薦饑，為慮更甚。

translations.literal: If famine is added on top, the concern is even greater.
translations.idiomatic: If famine follows as well, the danger is even greater.

sentences.zh: 時豪富之家，競為奢麗。

translations.literal: At that time wealthy and powerful families vied in extravagant luxury.
translations.idiomatic: At the time wealthy families competed in extravagant display.

sentences.zh: 季明又上書曰：

translations.literal: Jiming again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jiming submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞寬大所以兼覆，慈愛所以懷眾。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that breadth and largeness are what enable covering all; kindness and love are what enable embracing the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that breadth enables covering all, and kindness enables embracing the multitude.

sentences.zh: 故天地稱其高厚者，萬物得其容養焉；

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven and Earth are called high and thick because the ten thousand things receive their shelter and nurture;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth are called high and thick because the ten thousand things receive shelter and nurture from them;

sentences.zh: 四時著其寒暑者，庶類資其忠信焉。

translations.literal: the four seasons display their cold and heat because the myriad kinds rely on their constancy and trust.
translations.idiomatic: the four seasons show cold and heat because all living kinds rely on their constancy and good faith.

sentences.zh: 是以帝王者，寬大象天地，忠信則四時。

translations.literal: Thus emperors and kings take Heaven and Earth as their model of breadth, and the four seasons as their constancy and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Thus emperors and kings model themselves on the breadth of Heaven and Earth and the good faith of the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 招搖東指，天下識其春；

translations.literal: When the Dipper points east, all under Heaven knows it is spring;
translations.idiomatic: When the Dipper points east, all under Heaven knows spring has come;

sentences.zh: 人君布德，率土懷其惠。

translations.literal: when a ruler spreads virtue, all within the realm cherishes his grace.
translations.idiomatic: when a ruler spreads virtue, the realm cherishes his grace.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，資乾禦宇，品物咸亨，時乘六龍，自強不息，好問受規，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Bow low: Your Majesty, endowed with Heaven's potency, governs the universe; all things flourish. You ride the six dragons, strengthen yourself without cease, love to ask and receive remonstrance—the realm is greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, endowed with Heaven's potency, governs all things in prosperity, rides the six dragons without cease, and loves to ask and receive remonstrance—the realm is greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 自古至道之君，亦皆廣延博訪，詢采皞蕘，置鼓樹木，以求其過。

translations.literal: From antiquity the rulers of utmost Way have all broadly extended invitations and sought counsel, gathering even the words of grass cutters, setting up drums and trees to welcome criticism, to seek out their faults.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity rulers of utmost virtue have sought counsel widely, even from the humblest, and welcomed criticism to learn their faults.

sentences.zh: 頃者亢旱逾時，人懷望歲，陛下爰發明詔，廣求六瘼，同禹、湯之罪己，高宋景之守正，澍雨應時，年穀斯稔。

translations.literal: In recent years drought lasted beyond its season; people harbored hope for the year's harvest. Your Majesty then issued a brilliant edict, broadly seeking the six afflictions of the people, matching Yu and Tang in blaming themselves and rising to Song Jing in holding to the upright; timely rain responded, and the year's grain ripened.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years drought lasted beyond its season and the people hoped for rain. Your Majesty issued a brilliant edict seeking the people's afflictions, matching Yu and Tang in blaming yourself and Song Jing in holding to the upright; timely rain came and the year's grain ripened.

sentences.zh: 克己節用，慕質去華，此則尚矣。

translations.literal: Restraining oneself and economizing, admiring simplicity and detesting splendor—this is already lofty.
translations.idiomatic: You restrained yourself and economized, admired simplicity and detested extravagance—this is already lofty.

sentences.zh: 然而硃紫仍耀于衢路，綺縠猶侈于豪富，短褐未充於細人，糟糠未厭於編戶。

translations.literal: Yet crimson and purple still blaze on the roads, and fine silks are still extravagant in wealthy houses; coarse cloth does not fill the common people, and chaff and husks do not satisfy registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Yet crimson and purple still blaze on the roads, fine silks still adorn wealthy houses, coarse cloth does not clothe the common people, and coarse grain does not fill their bowls.

sentences.zh: 此則勸導之理，有所未周故也。

translations.literal: This is because the principle of guidance and leading has not yet been fully applied.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that guidance and persuasion have not yet reached everywhere.

sentences.zh: 今雖導之以禮，齊之以刑，風俗固難以一矣。

translations.literal: Now though you guide them with ritual and align them with punishments, custom is hard to make one.
translations.idiomatic: Though you guide them with ritual and align them with punishments, custom is hard to unify at once.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝集上書之囊，以作帷帳；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han gathered the bags of memorials to make curtains;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han gathered memorial bags to make curtains;

sentences.zh: 惜十家之產，不造露臺。

translations.literal: he prized the wealth of ten households and would not build the open terrace;
translations.idiomatic: he would not build a terrace that cost the wealth of ten households;

sentences.zh: 後宮所幸，衣不曳地，方之今日富室之飾，嘗不如婢隸之服。

translations.literal: those favored in the rear palace wore robes that did not trail on the ground—compared with the adornment of rich houses today, they were not even like servants' dress.
translations.idiomatic: palace women wore robes that did not trail on the ground—compared with rich houses today, even servants dress more lavishly.

sentences.zh: 然而以身率下，國富刑清，廟稱太宗，良有以也。

translations.literal: Yet by taking the body to lead those below, the state grew rich and punishments were clear; the temple calls him Emperor Taizong—and rightly so.
translations.idiomatic: By leading through his own example the state grew rich and punishments were clear; the temple honors him as Emperor Taizong, and rightly so.

sentences.zh: 臣聞聖人久于其道而天下化成。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when the sage long abides in the Way, all under Heaven is transformed.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage long abides in the Way, all under Heaven is transformed.

sentences.zh: 今承魏氏衰亂之後，貞信未興。

translations.literal: Now, inheriting the age after Wei's disorders, constancy and trust have not yet arisen.
translations.idiomatic: Now, after the disorders of Wei, constancy and trust have not yet been restored.

sentences.zh: 宜先尊五美，屏四惡，革浮華之俗，抑流競之風，察鴻都之小藝，焚雉頭之異服，無益之貨勿重于時，虧德之器勿陳於側，則人知德矣。

translations.literal: One should first follow the five beauties and banish the four evils, reform the custom of empty show, restrain the wind of reckless competition, examine the minor arts of Hongdu, burn the strange garments of pheasant-head style, let goods of no benefit not be prized in the age, and vessels that harm virtue not be displayed at the side—then the people will know virtue.
translations.idiomatic: First follow the five beauties and banish the four evils: reform empty display, restrain reckless competition, examine minor arts, burn outlandish dress, let useless goods not be prized, and harmful luxuries not be displayed—then the people will know virtue.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之，為政之要，在於選舉。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that the essential of governing lies in selection and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The essential of governing lies in selection and appointment.

sentences.zh: 若差之毫釐，則有千里之失；

translations.literal: If there is a hairsbreadth of error, there will be a thousand-li mistake;
translations.idiomatic: A hairsbreadth of error leads to a thousand-li mistake;

sentences.zh: 後來居上，則致積薪之譏。

translations.literal: If later men rise above their seniors, they incur the reproach of piling fuel upon fuel.
translations.idiomatic: If inferiors outrank their seniors, they invite the reproach of heaping fuel upon fuel.

sentences.zh: 是以古之善為政者，貫魚以次，任必以能。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients who governed well advanced men in order like a string of fish and always assigned office according to ability.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients who governed well advanced men in proper sequence, like fish strung on a line, and always assigned office according to ability.

sentences.zh: 爵人於朝，不以私愛。

translations.literal: They ennobled men at court without favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: They ennobled men at court without private favoritism.

sentences.zh: 簡才以授其官，量能以任其用。

translations.literal: They selected talent to grant office and measured capacity to assign duties.
translations.idiomatic: They selected talent for office and measured capacity for duty.

sentences.zh: 官得其才，任當其用，六轡既調，坐致千里。

translations.literal: When office obtained the right talent and assignment matched capacity, the six reins were tuned and a thousand li could be reached while seated.
translations.idiomatic: When office held the right talent and assignment matched capacity, the six reins were tuned and a thousand li could be reached without rising from the seat.

sentences.zh: 虞舜選眾，不仁者遠，則庶事康哉，人知其化矣。

translations.literal: When Yu Shun chose from among the multitude and the unworthy stood far off, then the myriad affairs were well ordered and men knew his transforming power.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Shun chose from among the multitude and the unworthy stood far off, the myriad affairs were well ordered and the people knew his transforming power.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and commended him.

sentences.zh: 時外史廨宇屢移，未有定所。

translations.literal: At that time the offices of the outer historians were repeatedly moved and had no fixed site.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the outer historians’ offices were repeatedly relocated and had no fixed site.

sentences.zh: 季明又上言曰：「外史之職，漢之東觀，帝王所寶，此焉攸在。

translations.literal: Jiming again submitted a memorial, saying, “The office of outer historian is the Eastern Pavilion of Han—what emperors treasure is preserved here.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming submitted another memorial: “The office of outer historian corresponds to the Eastern Pavilion of Han—what emperors treasure is kept here.

sentences.zh: 自魏及周，公館不立，臣雖愚瞽，猶知其非。

translations.literal: From Wei through Zhou no public hall was established; though I am foolish and blind, I still know this was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei through Zhou no public hall was established; though I am foolish and blind, I still know this was wrong.

sentences.zh: 是以去年十一月中，敢冒奏陳，特降中旨，即遣修營。

translations.literal: Therefore in the eleventh month of last year I dared to memorialize, and a special edict descended ordering construction at once.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the eleventh month of last year I dared memorialize, and a special edict descended ordering construction at once.

sentences.zh: 荏苒一周，未知功力。

translations.literal: A year has passed and the work accomplished is still unknown.
translations.idiomatic: A full year has passed and the progress of the work is still unknown.

sentences.zh: 臣職思其憂，敢不重請。

translations.literal: My office weighs upon my mind; I dare again to press the request.
translations.idiomatic: The duties of my office weigh upon my mind; I dare press the request again.

sentences.zh: 」帝納焉，於是廨宇方立。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it, and only then were the offices established.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted it, and only then were the offices established.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 又周文初，屬天下分崩，時學術之士蓋寡，故曲學末伎，咸見引納。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the early years of Emperor Wen of Zhou, when the realm was sundered, scholars were few; therefore crooked learning and petty skills were all brought in and employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years of Emperor Wen of Zhou, when the realm was sundered, scholars were few; crooked learning and petty skills were therefore all brought in and employed.

sentences.zh: 至若冀俊、趙文深之徒，雖才愧昔人，而名著於世，並見收用。

translations.literal: As for men such as Ji Jun and Zhao Wenshen, though their talent fell short of the men of old, their names were renowned in the age and they were all received and used.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Ji Jun and Zhao Wenshen, though their talent fell short of the men of old, were renowned in their age and were all received and employed.

sentences.zh: 冀俊，字僧俊，太原陽邑人也。

translations.literal: Ji Jun, styled Sengjun, was a native of Yangyi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Jun, styled Sengjun, came from Yangyi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 性沈謹，善隸書，特工模寫。

translations.literal: By nature he was reserved and careful, skilled in clerical script, and especially expert at imitation and copying.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was reserved and careful, skilled in clerical script, and especially expert at imitation and copying.

sentences.zh: 初為賀拔岳墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a staff officer in the Ink Office under Heba Yue.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as a staff officer in the Ink Office under Heba Yue.

sentences.zh: 岳被害，周文引為記室。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed, Emperor Wen of Zhou took him on as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was killed, Emperor Wen of Zhou took him on as recorder.

sentences.zh: 時周文志平侯莫陳悅，乃令俊偽為魏帝敕書與費也頭，令將兵助周文討悅。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wen wished to pacify Hou Mo Chen Yue and ordered Jun to forge an imperial edict of the Wei emperor to the Feiye’er tribe, commanding them to lead troops to aid Emperor Wen in attacking Yue.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Wen wished to pacify Hou Mo Chen Yue and ordered Jun to forge an imperial edict of the Wei emperor to the Feiye’er tribe, commanding them to lead troops to aid him in attacking Yue.

sentences.zh: 俊尋舊敕模寫，及代舍人、主書等署，與真無異。

translations.literal: Jun copied according to old edicts and substituted the signatures of the attendant secretaries and chief clerks, so that it was indistinguishable from the genuine.
translations.idiomatic: Jun copied from old edicts and substituted the signatures of the attendant secretaries and chief clerks, so that it was indistinguishable from the genuine.

sentences.zh: 周文大悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 費也頭見敕，不以為疑，遂遣兵受周文節度。

translations.literal: The Feiye’er saw the edict and had no suspicion, and so sent troops to accept Emperor Wen’s command.
translations.idiomatic: The Feiye’er saw the edict and had no suspicion, and sent troops to accept Emperor Wen’s command.

sentences.zh: 大統初，封長安縣男，從征弘農，戰于沙苑，進爵為子。

translations.literal: In the early Dazong era he was enfeoffed as Baron of Chang’an; he followed the campaign against Hongnong and fought at Shaye, and was advanced in rank to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dazong era he was enfeoffed as Baron of Chang’an; he followed the campaign against Hongnong and fought at Shaye, and was advanced to viscount.

sentences.zh: 累遷襄樂郡守。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Xiangyue.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Xiangyue.

sentences.zh: 尋征還，教明帝及宋獻公等隸書。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and instructed Emperor Ming and Duke Xian of Song and others in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled and instructed Emperor Ming and Duke Xian of Song and others in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 時俗入書學者亦行束修之禮，謂之謝章。

translations.literal: At that time those who entered schools of calligraphy also observed the ceremony of presenting dried meat, which was called the “letter of thanks.”
translations.idiomatic: At that time those who entered schools of calligraphy also observed the ceremony of presenting dried meat, called the “letter of thanks.”

sentences.zh: 俊以書字所興，起自蒼頡，若同常俗，未為合禮，遂啟周文，釋奠蒼頡及先聖、先師。

translations.literal: Jun held that because writing arose with Cang Jie, to follow ordinary custom would not accord with ritual; he therefore memorialized Emperor Wen to offer sacrifices to Cang Jie and to the Former Sage and Former Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Jun held that because writing arose with Cang Jie, to follow ordinary custom would not accord with ritual; he therefore memorialized Emperor Wen to offer sacrifices to Cang Jie and to the Former Sage and Former Teacher.

sentences.zh: 除黃門侍郎、本州大中正。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant and chief rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Palace Attendant and chief rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 累遷湖州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 靜退，每以清約自處。

translations.literal: Quiet and retiring, he always maintained himself in frugal purity.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and retiring, he always maintained himself in frugal purity.

sentences.zh: 前後所曆，頗有聲稱。

translations.literal: In the offices he successively held, he won a fair reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In the offices he successively held, he won a fair reputation.

sentences.zh: 尋加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was soon additionally made General of Agile Cavalry and Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally made General of Agile Cavalry and Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 後進爵為昌樂侯，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was advanced in rank to Marquis of Changle and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later advanced to Marquis of Changle and died.

sentences.zh: 趙文深，字德本，南陽宛人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Wenshen, styled Deben, was a native of Wan in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenshen, styled Deben, came from Wan in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 父遐，以醫術仕魏，為尚藥典禦。

translations.literal: His father Xia served Wei with medical skill as Director of the Palace Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xia served Wei with medical skill as Director of the Palace Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 文深少學楷隸。

translations.literal: Wenshen in youth studied regular and clerical scripts.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshen in youth studied regular and clerical scripts.

sentences.zh: 年十一，獻書于魏帝。

translations.literal: At eleven he presented a writing to the Wei emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he presented a writing to the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 後立義歸朝，除大丞相府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: Later he raised righteous troops and submitted to the court, and was appointed legal staff officer in the Grand Chancellor’s headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later he raised righteous troops and submitted to the court, and was appointed legal staff officer in the Grand Chancellor’s headquarters.

sentences.zh: 雅有鐘、王之則，筆勢可觀。

translations.literal: He had the standards of Zhong and Wang in elegance, and his brushwork was admirable.
translations.idiomatic: He had the standards of Zhong and Wang in elegance, and his brushwork was admirable.

sentences.zh: 當時碑榜，唯文深、冀俊而已。

translations.literal: At that time for steles and placards only Wenshen and Ji Jun were employed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time for steles and placards only Wenshen and Ji Jun were employed.

sentences.zh: 大統十二年，追論立義功，封白石縣男。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dazong, in reckoning merit for raising righteous troops, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Dazong, in reckoning merit for raising righteous troops, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Baishi.

sentences.zh: 文帝以隸書紕繆，命文深與黎季明、沈遐等依《說文》及《字林》，刊定六體，成一萬餘言，行於世。

translations.literal: Because clerical script was erroneous, Emperor Wen ordered Wenshen, together with Li Jiming and Shen Xia and others, to collate the six scripts according to the Shuowen and the Zilin, producing more than ten thousand characters that circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Because clerical script was erroneous, Emperor Wen ordered Wenshen, together with Li Jiming and Shen Xia and others, to collate the six scripts according to the Shuowen and the Zilin, producing more than ten thousand characters that circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 及平江陵之後，王褒入關，貴遊等翕然並學褒書。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Jiangling, Wang Bao entered the Pass, and the nobility all at once studied Bao’s calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Jiangling, Wang Bao entered the Pass, and the nobility all at once studied Bao’s calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 文深之書，遂被遐棄。

translations.literal: Wenshen’s writing was then cast far behind.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshen’s writing was then cast far behind.

sentences.zh: 文深慚恨，形於言色。

translations.literal: Wenshen’s resentment showed in his words and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshen’s resentment showed in his words and countenance.

sentences.zh: 後知好尚難及，亦改習褒書。

translations.literal: Later, knowing that the prevailing taste was hard to match, he also changed to studying Bao’s script.
translations.idiomatic: Later, knowing that prevailing taste was hard to match, he also changed to studying Bao’s script.

sentences.zh: 然竟無所成，轉被譏議，謂之學步邯鄲焉。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he achieved nothing and was turned to ridicule, called one who imitated the Handan gait.
