translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he achieved nothing and was ridiculed as one who imitated the Handan gait.

sentences.zh: 至於碑榜，余人猶莫之逮。

translations.literal: As for steles and placards, others still could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: As for steles and placards, others still could not match him.

sentences.zh: 王褒亦每推先之。

translations.literal: Wang Bao also always gave him precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao also always gave him precedence.

sentences.zh: 宮殿樓閣，皆其跡也。

translations.literal: Palaces, towers, and pavilions all bear traces of his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces, towers, and pavilions all bear traces of his hand.

sentences.zh: 遷縣伯下大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Grand Master with the rank of district marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Grand Master with the rank of district marquis.

sentences.zh: 明帝令至江陵書影覆寺碑，漢南人士，亦以為工。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming ordered him to go to Jiangling to write the stele of the Yingfu Temple, and the gentlemen of Hannan also deemed it accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered him to Jiangling to write the stele of the Yingfu Temple, and the gentlemen of Hannan also deemed it accomplished.

sentences.zh: 梁主蕭察觀而美之，賞遺甚厚。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler Xiao Cha viewed it and admired it, rewarding him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler Xiao Cha viewed it and admired it, rewarding him very generously.

sentences.zh: 天和元年，露寢等初成，文深以題榜之功，除趙興郡守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, when the Lumen dormitory and other buildings were first completed, Wenshen was made Administrator of Zhaoxing for his merit in inscribing the placards.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianhe, when the Lumen dormitory and other buildings were first completed, Wenshen was made Administrator of Zhaoxing for his merit in inscribing the placards.

sentences.zh: 文深雖居外任，每須題榜，輒復追之。

translations.literal: Though Wenshen held an outer post, whenever placards were needed he was again summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wenshen held an outer post, whenever placards were needed he was summoned back.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，除太常少卿，改封任城郡公，進位開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was appointed Vice Minister of Ceremonies, his fief changed to Duke of Rencheng, and he was advanced to Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was appointed Vice Minister of Ceremonies, his fief changed to Duke of Rencheng, and he was advanced to Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 曆國子祭酒、禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Chancellor of the National University and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He successively held the posts of Chancellor of the National University and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 與秘書監牛弘撰新禮。

translations.literal: Together with the Director of the Secretariat Niu Hong he compiled the new rites.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the Director of the Secretariat Niu Hong he compiled the new rites.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗令彥之與沈重論議，重不能抗，避席而謝曰：「辛君所謂金城湯池，無可攻之勢。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered Yanzhi to debate with Shen Chong; Chong could not withstand him, rose from his mat, and apologized, saying, “What Lord Xin calls a golden rampart and boiling moat has no point that can be attacked.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered Yanzhi to debate with Shen Chong; Chong could not withstand him, rose from his mat, and apologized, saying, “What Lord Xin calls a golden rampart and boiling moat has no point that can be attacked.”

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 後除隨州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 時州牧多貢珍玩，惟彥之所貢，並供祭之類。

translations.literal: At that time most governors presented rare curiosities, but what Yanzhi presented consisted entirely of items for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At that time most governors presented rare curiosities, but what Yanzhi presented consisted entirely of items for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 上謂朝臣曰：「人安得無學！

translations.literal: The emperor said to the court officials, “How can a man do without learning!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the court officials, “How can a man do without learning!

sentences.zh: 彥之所貢，稽古之力也。

translations.literal: What Yanzhi presented shows the force of investigating antiquity.”
translations.idiomatic: What Yanzhi presented shows the force of investigating antiquity.”

sentences.zh: 」遷潞州刺史，前後俱有惠政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Luzhou, and in both posts he had benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Luzhou, and in both posts he had benevolent government.

sentences.zh: 彥之又崇信佛道，於城內立浮圖二所，並十五層。

translations.literal: Yanzhi also deeply honored the Buddhist Way and erected within the city two pagodas of fifteen stories each.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi also deeply honored the Buddhist Way and erected within the city two pagodas of fifteen stories each.

sentences.zh: 開皇十一年，州人張元暴死，數日乃蘇。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang, Zhang Yuan of the province suddenly died and after several days revived.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang, Zhang Yuan of the province suddenly died and after several days revived.

sentences.zh: 雲遊天上，見新構一堂，制極崇麗。

translations.literal: He said he traveled in Heaven and saw a newly built hall of utmost splendor.
translations.idiomatic: He said he traveled in Heaven and saw a newly built hall of utmost splendor.

sentences.zh: 元問其故，雲潞州刺史辛彥之有功德，造此堂以待之。

translations.literal: Yuan asked the reason; he was told that Governor Xin Yanzhi of Luzhou had merit, and this hall was built to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan asked the reason; he was told that Governor Xin Yanzhi of Luzhou had merit, and this hall was built to await him.

sentences.zh: 彥之聞而不悅。

translations.literal: Yanzhi heard it and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi heard it and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died that year, and his posthumous title was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year, and his posthumous title was Xuan.

sentences.zh: 彥之撰《墳典》一部、《六官》一部、《祝文》一部、《禮耍》一部、《新禮》一部、《五經異義》一部，並行於世。

translations.literal: Yanzhi authored one work each on the Canon of Documents, the Six Offices, Prayer Texts, Essentials of Rites, New Rites, and Differences of Opinion on the Five Classics, all of which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi authored one work each on the Canon of Documents, the Six Offices, Prayer Texts, Essentials of Rites, New Rites, and Differences of Opinion on the Five Classics, all of which circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 子孝舒、仲龕，並早有令譽。

translations.literal: His sons Xiaoshu and Zhongqian both early won fine reputations.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xiaoshu and Zhongqian both early won fine reputations.

sentences.zh: 何妥，字棲風，西城人也。

translations.literal: He Tuo, styled Qifeng, was a native of Xicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He Tuo, styled Qifeng, came from Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 父細腳胡，通商入蜀，遂家郫縣。

translations.literal: His father was a Sogdian merchant who traded into Shu and then made his home in Pixian.
translations.idiomatic: His father was a Sogdian merchant who traded into Shu and then made his home in Pixian.

sentences.zh: 事梁武陵王紀，主知金帛，因致巨富，號為西州大賈。

translations.literal: He served the Liang Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, as overseer of gold and silk, and thereby amassed great wealth, being called the greatest merchant of the Western Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Liang Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, as overseer of gold and silk, and thereby amassed great wealth, being called the greatest merchant of the Western Provinces.

sentences.zh: 妥少機警，八歲游國子學，助教顧良戲之曰：「汝姓何，是荷葉之荷？

translations.literal: Tuo was clever from youth; at eight he entered the Imperial Academy, and the assistant instructor Gu Liang teased him, saying, “Your surname He—is it the he of lotus leaf?
translations.idiomatic: Tuo was clever from youth; at eight he entered the Imperial Academy, and Assistant Instructor Gu Liang teased him, saying, “Your surname He—is it the he of lotus leaf?

sentences.zh: 為河水之河？

translations.literal: Or the he of river water?”
translations.idiomatic: Or the he of river water?”

sentences.zh: 」妥應聲答曰：「先生姓顧，是眷顧之顧？

translations.literal: Tuo answered at once, “Sir, your surname Gu—is it the gu of regard?
translations.idiomatic: Tuo answered at once, “Sir, your surname Gu—is it the gu of regard?

sentences.zh: 為新故之故？

translations.literal: Or the gu of old and new?”
translations.idiomatic: Or the gu of old and new?”

sentences.zh: 」眾咸異之。

translations.literal: The crowd all marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd all marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 十七，以伎巧事湘東王。

translations.literal: At seventeen he served the Prince of Xiangdong with skill in craft.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he served the Prince of Xiangdong with skill in craft.

sentences.zh: 後知其聰明，召為誦書左右。

translations.literal: Later, knowing his intelligence, the prince summoned him as a recitation attendant at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Later, knowing his intelligence, the prince summoned him as a recitation attendant at his side.

sentences.zh: 時蘭陵蕭翽，亦有俊才，住青楊巷，妥住白楊頭。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Xu of Lanling also had outstanding talent; Xu lived on Green Poplar Lane and Tuo lived at White Poplar Head.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Xu of Lanling also had outstanding talent; Xu lived on Green Poplar Lane and Tuo at White Poplar Head.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「世有兩俊，白楊何妥，青楊蕭翽。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: “In the age there are two outstanding men—He Tuo of White Poplar and Xiao Xu of Green Poplar.”
translations.idiomatic: People of the time made a saying of it: “In the age there are two outstanding men—He Tuo of White Poplar and Xiao Xu of Green Poplar.”

sentences.zh: 」其見美如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he admired.
translations.idiomatic: Thus was he admired.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，入周，仕為太學博士。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified he entered Zhou and served as Erudite of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling was pacified he entered Zhou and served as Erudite of the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 宣帝初立五後，問儒者辛彥之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan first established five empresses, he asked the Confucian Xin Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan first established five empresses, he asked the Confucian Xin Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「後與天子匹體齊尊，不宜有五。

translations.literal: He answered, “An empress shares the body and equal honor with the Son of Heaven; there should not be five.”
translations.idiomatic: He answered, “An empress shares the body and equal honor with the Son of Heaven; there should not be five.”

sentences.zh: 」妥駁曰：「帝嚳四妃，舜又二妃，亦何常數？

translations.literal: Tuo rebutted, saying, “Emperor Ku had four consorts and Shun again had two—what fixed number is there?”
translations.idiomatic: Tuo rebutted, saying, “Emperor Ku had four consorts and Shun again had two—what fixed number is there?”

sentences.zh: 」由是封襄城縣男。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，除國子博士，加通直散騎常侍，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, he was appointed Erudite of the National University, additionally made Regular Attendant at Large with direct access, and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, he was appointed Erudite of the National University, additionally made Regular Attendant at Large with direct access, and advanced in rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 妥姓勁急，有口才，好是非人物。

translations.literal: Tuo’s surname was forceful and urgent; he had a ready tongue and loved to pass judgment on others.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo’s nature was forceful and urgent; he had a ready tongue and loved to pass judgment on others.

sentences.zh: 納言蘇威嘗言於上曰：「臣先人每誡臣云：唯讀《孝經》一卷，足可立身經國，何用多為？

translations.literal: The Adviser Su Wei once said to the emperor, “My forefathers always admonished me, saying: to read only one juan of the Classic of Filial Piety is enough to establish oneself and govern the state—what need is there to read much?”
translations.idiomatic: Adviser Su Wei once said to the emperor, “My forefathers always admonished me: to read only one juan of the Classic of Filial Piety is enough to establish oneself and govern the state—what need is there to read much?”

sentences.zh: 」上亦然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 妥進曰：「蘇威所學，非止《孝經》。

translations.literal: Tuo advanced and said, "What Su Wei has studied is not limited to the Classic of Filial Piety alone.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo stepped forward and said, "Su Wei's learning is not limited to the Classic of Filial Piety alone.

sentences.zh: 厥父若信有此言，威不從訓，是其不孝；

translations.literal: If his father truly believed this saying and Wei did not follow the instruction, that is his lack of filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: If his father truly said this and Wei did not follow the teaching, that is unfilial;

sentences.zh: 若無此言，面欺陛下，是其不誠。

translations.literal: if there was no such saying, then to deceive Your Majesty to his face is his lack of sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: if there was no such saying, then to deceive Your Majesty to his face is insincerity.

sentences.zh: 不誠不孝，何以事君？

translations.literal: Lacking sincerity and filial piety—how can he serve his lord?
translations.idiomatic: Insincere and unfilial—how can he serve his lord?

sentences.zh: 且夫子又云：'不讀《詩》無以言，不讀《禮》無以立。

translations.literal: Moreover the Master also said: "Without reading the Odes one has no words; without reading the Rites one has no standing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Master also said: "Without reading the Odes one has nothing to say; without reading the Rites one has no footing.

sentences.zh: '豈容蘇綽教子，獨反聖人之訓乎？

translations.literal: How could Su Chuo in teaching his son alone go against the sage's instruction?
translations.idiomatic: How could Su Chuo alone, in teaching his son, go against the sage's instruction?

sentences.zh: 」威時兼領五職，上甚親重之。

translations.literal: At that time Wei concurrently held five offices, and the emperor held him in great favor and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei held five offices concurrently, and the emperor favored and esteemed him greatly.

sentences.zh: 妥因奏威不可信任。

translations.literal: Tuo thereupon memorialized that Wei could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo thereupon memorialized that Wei could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 又以掌天文律度，皆不稱職，妥上八事以諫。

translations.literal: He also said that in charge of astronomy and pitch-pipes he was altogether unfit for office, and Tuo submitted eight points in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that in astronomy and pitch-pipes Wei was altogether unfit for office, and Tuo submitted eight points in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 其一事曰：臣聞知人則哲，惟帝難之。

translations.literal: The first point said: Your servant has heard that to know men is to be wise—only the emperor finds it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The first point said: I have heard that to know men is wisdom—only the emperor finds it difficult.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：舉直錯枉則人服，舉枉錯直則人不服。

translations.literal: Confucius said: Raise the upright and set them above the crooked and the people will submit; raise the crooked and set them above the upright and the people will not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: Raise the upright and set them above the crooked and the people will submit; raise the crooked and set them above the upright and the people will not submit.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，政之安危，必慎所舉。

translations.literal: From this it follows that the safety or peril of government depends on being careful in whom one appoints.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that the safety or peril of government depends on whom one appoints.

sentences.zh: 故進賢受上賞，蔽賢蒙顯戮。

translations.literal: Therefore to advance the worthy receives the highest reward, while to screen the worthy incurs conspicuous punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to advance the worthy wins the highest reward, while to screen the worthy brings conspicuous punishment.

sentences.zh: 察今之舉人，良異於此。

translations.literal: Examining how men are appointed today, it is quite the opposite of this.
translations.idiomatic: Examining appointments today, the practice is quite the opposite.

sentences.zh: 無論諂直，莫擇賢愚。

translations.literal: Whether flatterers or the upright, none distinguishes worthy from unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterer or upright, none distinguishes worthy from unworthy.

sentences.zh: 心欲崇高，則起家喉舌之任；

translations.literal: If the heart desires eminence, one begins with the duties of the throat and tongue;
translations.idiomatic: If one desires eminence, one begins with the duties of the throat and tongue;

sentences.zh: 意須抑屈，必白首郎署之官。

translations.literal: if one must be kept down, one ends white-haired in an office of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: if one must be kept down, one ends white-haired in a secretariat post.

sentences.zh: 人不之服，實由於此。

translations.literal: That the people do not submit—truly it is owing to this.
translations.idiomatic: That the people do not submit is truly owing to this.

sentences.zh: 臣聞爵人於朝，與士共之；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that to ennoble a man at court is to share him with the gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to ennoble a man at court is to share him with the gentlemen;

sentences.zh: 刑人於市，與眾棄之。

translations.literal: to punish a man in the market is to cast him off with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: to punish a man in the market is to cast him off with the multitude.

sentences.zh: 伏見留心獄訟，愛人如子，每應決獄，無不詢訪群公，刑之不濫，君之明也。

translations.literal: I have observed that you attend carefully to lawsuits and love your people as sons; whenever you must judge cases, you never fail to consult the high ministers—punishment without excess is the ruler's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that you attend carefully to lawsuits and love your people as sons; whenever you judge a case, you consult the high ministers—punishment without excess is the mark of a clear-sighted ruler.

sentences.zh: 刑既如此。

translations.literal: Punishment has already been thus.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment is already thus.

sentences.zh: 爵亦宜然。

translations.literal: Rewards should likewise be so.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards should be the same.

sentences.zh: 若有懋功，簡在帝心者，便可擢用。

translations.literal: If there is outstanding merit and one is singled out in the emperor's heart, he may be promoted and employed at once.
translations.idiomatic: If there is outstanding merit and one is singled out in the emperor's heart, promote and employ him at once.

sentences.zh: 自斯以降，若選重官，必參以眾議，勿信一人之舉，則上不偏私，下無怨望。

translations.literal: From this point downward, if heavy offices are chosen, all deliberation must be consulted; do not trust a single man's nomination—then above there will be no partiality and below no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: From here on, when choosing high offices, consult broad deliberation; do not trust a single man's nomination—then above there will be no partiality and below no resentment.

sentences.zh: 其二事曰：孔子云：是察阿黨，則罪無掩蔽。

translations.literal: The second point said: Confucius said: Discern factions, and crimes cannot be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: The second point said: Confucius said: Discern factions, and crimes cannot be concealed.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「君子周而不比，小人比而不周。

translations.literal: He also said: "The gentleman is inclusive but does not form factions; the petty man forms factions but is not inclusive.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The gentleman is inclusive but does not form factions; the petty man forms factions but is not inclusive.

sentences.zh: 」所謂比者，即阿黨也。

translations.literal: What is called "forming factions" is precisely factional cliquing.
translations.idiomatic: What is called "forming factions" is precisely factional cliquing.

sentences.zh: 謂心之所愛，既已光華榮顯，猶加提挈；

translations.literal: Those whom the heart loves, though already splendid and honored, are still further elevated;
translations.idiomatic: Those whom the heart loves, though already splendid and honored, are still further elevated;

sentences.zh: 心之所惡，既已沈滯屈辱，薄言必怒。

translations.literal: those whom the heart hates, though already sunk low and humiliated, at the slightest word are met with wrath.
translations.idiomatic: those whom the heart hates, though already sunk low and humiliated, at the slightest word meet with wrath.

sentences.zh: 提挈既成，必相掩蔽，則欺上之心生矣；

translations.literal: Once elevation is accomplished, mutual concealment necessarily follows, and the heart to deceive one's superiors is born;
translations.idiomatic: Once elevation is accomplished, mutual concealment follows, and the heart to deceive one's superiors is born;

sentences.zh: 屈辱既加，則有怨恨，謗讟之言出矣。

translations.literal: once humiliation is added, resentment arises and words of slander go forth.
translations.idiomatic: once humiliation is added, resentment arises and slander goes forth.

sentences.zh: 伏願廣加訪察，勿使朋黨路開，威恩自任。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that you broadly increase investigation and scrutiny, and not let the path of factions be opened so that authority and favor are taken into one's own hands.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that you broaden investigation and not let the path of factions open so that authority and favor are taken into one's own hands.

sentences.zh: 有國之患，莫大於此。

translations.literal: For one who holds a state, there is no affliction greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: For one who holds a state, there is no affliction greater than this.

sentences.zh: 其三事曰：臣聞舜舉十六族，所謂八元八凱也。

translations.literal: The third point said: Your servant has heard that Shun raised sixteen clans—the so-called Eight Worthies and Eight Heroes.
translations.idiomatic: The third point said: I have heard that Shun raised sixteen clans—the so-called Eight Worthies and Eight Heroes.

sentences.zh: 計其賢明，理優今日。

translations.literal: Considering their worth and wisdom, they were in principle superior to men of today.
translations.idiomatic: Considering their worth and wisdom, they were in principle superior to men of today.

sentences.zh: 猶復擇才授任，不相侵濫。

translations.literal: Yet he still chose talent and assigned duties, without mutual encroachment or excess.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still chose talent and assigned duties without mutual encroachment or excess.

sentences.zh: 故得四門雍穆，庶績咸熙。

translations.literal: Therefore the four gates were harmonious and all achievements flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the four gates were harmonious and all achievements flourished.

sentences.zh: 今官員極多，用人甚少，一人身上，乃兼數職。

translations.literal: Today officials are extremely numerous but employment is very slight—on a single person several offices are piled.
translations.idiomatic: Today officials are extremely numerous but few are employed—on a single person several offices are piled.

sentences.zh: 為是國無人也？

translations.literal: Is it because the state has no men?
translations.idiomatic: Is it because the state has no men?

sentences.zh: 為是人不善也？

translations.literal: Or because the men are not good?
translations.idiomatic: Or because the men are not good?

sentences.zh: 今萬乘大國，髦彥不少，縱有明哲，無由自達。

translations.literal: Now in a great state of ten thousand chariots outstanding talents are not few; yet even if there are wise and clear-minded men, they have no way to advance themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Now in a great state of ten thousand chariots outstanding talents are not few; yet even the wise and clear-minded have no way to advance themselves.

sentences.zh: 東方朔言曰：「尊之則為將，卑之則為虜。

translations.literal: Dongfang Shuo said: "Honor a man and he becomes a general; degrade him and he becomes a captive.
translations.idiomatic: Dongfang Shuo said: "Honor a man and he becomes a general; degrade him and he becomes a captive.

sentences.zh: 」斯言信矣。

translations.literal: This saying is indeed true.
translations.idiomatic: That saying is indeed true.

sentences.zh: 今當官之人，不度德量力，既無呂望、傅說之能，自負傅岩、渭水之氣。

translations.literal: Those who hold office today do not measure virtue and weigh capacity; lacking the ability of Lü Wang or Fu Yue, they yet pride themselves on the air of Fuyan and the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold office today do not measure virtue and weigh capacity; lacking the ability of Lü Wang or Fu Yue, they yet pride themselves on the air of Fuyan and the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 不慮憂深責重，唯畏總領不多。

translations.literal: They do not consider that cares are deep and burdens heavy; they only fear that their overall superintendence is not extensive enough.
translations.idiomatic: They do not consider that cares are deep and burdens heavy; they only fear that their overall charge is not extensive enough.

sentences.zh: 安斯寵任，輕彼權軸。

translations.literal: Content with such favor and appointment, they treat lightly the axle of power.
translations.idiomatic: Content with such favor and appointment, they treat lightly the axle of power.

sentences.zh: 顛沛致蹶，實此之由。

translations.literal: That overturning and stumbling to a fall—truly it comes from this.
translations.idiomatic: Overturning and falling—truly it comes from this.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「鼎折足，覆公餗，其形渥，凶。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "The cauldron's legs break; the lord's stew is overturned; his person is stained—misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "The cauldron's legs break; the lord's stew is overturned; his person is stained—misfortune.

sentences.zh: 」言不勝其任也。

translations.literal: It speaks of not being equal to one's charge.
translations.idiomatic: It speaks of not being equal to one's charge.

sentences.zh: 臣聞窮力舉重，不能為用。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that to exhaust one's strength in lifting a heavy weight cannot be made useful.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to exhaust one's strength lifting a heavy weight cannot be made useful.

sentences.zh: 伏願更任賢良，分才參掌，使各行其力，則庶事康哉。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that you reassign the worthy and good, divide talents and share in governance, and let each exert his strength—then the myriad affairs will be well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that you reassign the worthy and good, divide talents and share governance, and let each exert his strength—then the myriad affairs will be well ordered.

sentences.zh: 其四事曰：臣聞《禮》云：析言破律，亂名改作，執左道以亂政者殺。

translations.literal: The fourth point said: Your servant has heard the Rites say: To twist words and break statutes, to disorder names and alter institutions, to hold to heterodox ways and disorder government—such men are put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth point said: I have heard the Rites say: To twist words and break statutes, to disorder names and alter institutions, to hold to heterodox ways and disorder government—such men are put to death.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：仍舊貫，何必改作。

translations.literal: Confucius said: Follow the old pattern—why must one alter and remake?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: Follow the old pattern—why alter and remake?

sentences.zh: 伏見比年以來，改作者多矣。

translations.literal: I have observed that in recent years those who alter and remake have been many.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that in recent years those who alter and remake have been many.

sentences.zh: 如範威刻漏，十載不成；

translations.literal: Such as Fan Wei's clepsydra—in ten years it was not completed;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wei's clepsydra took ten years and was still not completed;

sentences.zh: 趙翊尺秤，七年方決；

translations.literal: Zhao Yi's yard-measure and scales—only after seven years was it settled;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi's yard-measure and scales were settled only after seven years;

sentences.zh: 公孫濟迂誕，醫方費逾巨萬；

translations.literal: Gongsun Ji's pedantry and extravagance—medical prescriptions cost more than ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Ji's pedantry and extravagance cost more than ten thousand in medical prescriptions;

sentences.zh: 徐道慶回互子午，糜耗飲食；

translations.literal: Xu Daoqing's twisting of the noon and midnight hours squandered food and drink;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daoqing's twisting of the noon and midnight hours squandered food and drink;

sentences.zh: 常明破律，多曆歲時；

translations.literal: Chang Ming's breaking of statutes lasted many years;
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ming's breaking of statutes lasted many years;

sentences.zh: 王渥亂名，曾無紀極；

translations.literal: Wang Wo's disordering of names knew no limit;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wo's disordering of names knew no limit;

sentences.zh: 張山居未知星位，前已蹂藉太常；

translations.literal: Zhang Shanju did not know the star positions—before he had already trampled the Grand Steward;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shanju did not know the star positions—before, he had already trampled the Grand Steward;

sentences.zh: 曹魏祖不識北辰，今復晳蘭轢太史。

translations.literal: Cao Weizu did not recognize the North Star—now again he crushes the Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Weizu did not recognize the North Star—now again he crushes the Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 莫不用其短見，便自誇毗，邀射名譽，厚相誣罔。

translations.literal: None fails to employ his shallow views, then boast to neighbors, seek to score reputation, and thickly deceive one another.
translations.idiomatic: None fails to employ his shallow views, boast to neighbors, seek reputation, and thickly deceive one another.

sentences.zh: 請今日已後，有如此者，若其言不驗，必加重罰。

translations.literal: I beg that from today onward, when there are such men, if their words are not verified, they must receive increased punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that from today onward, when there are such men, if their words are not verified, punishment be increased.

sentences.zh: 庶令有所畏忌，不敢輕奏狂簡。

translations.literal: So that they may have something to fear and not dare lightly submit wild and coarse memorials.
translations.idiomatic: So that they may have something to fear and not dare lightly submit wild and coarse memorials.

sentences.zh: 其餘文多不載。

translations.literal: The remaining text is mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder is mostly not recorded.

sentences.zh: 時蘇威權兼數職，先嘗隱武功，故妥言「自負傅岩、渭水之氣」，以此激上。

translations.literal: At that time Su Wei held several offices by concurrent appointment; he had earlier concealed his military achievements, so Tuo's words about "priding oneself on the air of Fuyan and the Wei River" were meant to provoke the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Su Wei held several offices concurrently; he had earlier concealed his military achievements, so Tuo's words about "priding oneself on the air of Fuyan and the Wei River" were meant to provoke the emperor.

sentences.zh: 書奏，威大銜之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Wei deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Wei deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 二年，威定考文學，妥更相訶詆。

translations.literal: In the second year, when Wei set the assessments for literary scholars, Tuo and he again mutually reviled each other.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Wei set the assessments for literary scholars, Tuo and he again reviled each other.

sentences.zh: 威勃然曰：「無何妥，不慮無博士！

translations.literal: Wei said in rage: "Without He Tuo, I do not worry that there will be no erudites!
translations.idiomatic: Wei said in rage: "Without He Tuo, I do not worry that there will be no erudites!

sentences.zh: 」妥應聲曰：「無蘇威，亦何憂無執事！

translations.literal: Tuo answered on the spot: "Without Su Wei, what worry is there of having no chief administrator!
translations.idiomatic: Tuo answered on the spot: "Without Su Wei, what worry is there of having no chief administrator!

sentences.zh: 」於是與威有隙。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had a breach with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he had a breach with Wei.

sentences.zh: 其後，上令妥考定鐘律。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor ordered Tuo to examine and fix the bells and pitch-pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the emperor ordered Tuo to examine and fix the bells and pitch-pipes.

sentences.zh: 妥又上表曰：

translations.literal: Tuo again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tuo again submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: when manifest there are rites and music; when hidden there are ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard: when manifest there are rites and music; when hidden there are ghosts and spirits.

sentences.zh: 然則動天地，感鬼神，莫近于禮樂。

translations.literal: Thus to move Heaven and earth and touch ghosts and spirits, nothing is closer than rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: To move Heaven and earth and touch ghosts and spirits, nothing is closer than rites and music.

sentences.zh: 又云：樂至則無怨，禮至則不爭。

translations.literal: It is also said: when music reaches its utmost there is no resentment; when rites reach their utmost there is no contention.
translations.idiomatic: It is also said: when music reaches its utmost there is no resentment; when rites reach their utmost there is no contention.

sentences.zh: 揖讓而臨天下者，禮樂之謂也。

translations.literal: To rule all under Heaven through bowing and yielding—that is what rites and music mean.
translations.idiomatic: To rule all under Heaven through bowing and yielding—that is what rites and music mean.

sentences.zh: 臣聞樂有二：一曰奸聲，二曰正聲。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that music has two kinds: one called corrupt sound, one called correct sound.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that music has two kinds: one called corrupt sound, one called correct sound.

sentences.zh: 夫奸聲感人而逆氣應之，正聲感人而順氣應之。

translations.literal: Corrupt sound moves people and contrary qi responds; correct sound moves people and harmonious qi responds.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt sound moves people and contrary qi responds; correct sound moves people and harmonious qi responds.

sentences.zh: 順氣成象，故樂行而倫清，耳目聰明，血氣和平，移風易俗，天下皆寧。

translations.literal: When harmonious qi forms images, therefore music proceeds and relationships are clear, ears and eyes are keen, blood and breath are peaceful, customs are transformed and habits changed, and all under Heaven is tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: When harmonious qi forms images, music proceeds and relationships are clear, ears and eyes are keen, blood and breath are peaceful, customs are transformed, and all under Heaven is tranquil.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「放鄭聲，遠佞人。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Banish the sounds of Zheng; keep sycophants at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Banish the sounds of Zheng; keep sycophants at a distance.

sentences.zh: 」故鄭、衛、宋、趙之聲出，內則發疾，外則傷人。

translations.literal: Therefore when the sounds of Zheng, Wei, Song, and Zhao appear, inwardly they produce illness; outwardly they harm people.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the sounds of Zheng, Wei, Song, and Zhao appear, inwardly they produce illness; outwardly they harm people.

sentences.zh: 是以宮亂則荒，其君驕；

translations.literal: Thus if gong is disordered, there is desolation and the ruler becomes arrogant;
translations.idiomatic: If gong is disordered, there is desolation and the ruler becomes arrogant;

sentences.zh: 商亂則破，其官壞；

translations.literal: if shang is disordered, there is collapse and the ministers are ruined;
translations.idiomatic: if shang is disordered, there is collapse and the ministers are ruined;

sentences.zh: 角亂則憂，其人怨；

translations.literal: if jue is disordered, there is grief and the people resent;
translations.idiomatic: if jue is disordered, there is grief and the people resent;

sentences.zh: 徵亂則哀，其事勤；

translations.literal: if zhi is disordered, there is sorrow and affairs are labored;
translations.idiomatic: if zhi is disordered, there is sorrow and affairs are labored;

sentences.zh: 羽亂則危，其財匱。

translations.literal: if yu is disordered, there is peril and wealth is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: if yu is disordered, there is peril and wealth is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 五者皆亂，則國亡無日矣。

translations.literal: If all five are disordered, the state will perish without delay.
translations.idiomatic: If all five are disordered, the state will perish without delay.

sentences.zh: 魏文侯問子夏曰：「吾端冕而聽古樂，則欲寐；

translations.literal: Marquis Wen of Wei asked Zixia, saying: "When I wear my cap and robe and listen to ancient music, I want to sleep;
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Wen of Wei asked Zixia: "When I wear my cap and robe and listen to ancient music, I want to sleep;

sentences.zh: 聽鄭衛之音而不倦，何也？

translations.literal: when I listen to the sounds of Zheng and Wei I am not weary—why?
translations.idiomatic: when I listen to the sounds of Zheng and Wei I am not weary—why?

sentences.zh: 」子夏對曰：「夫古樂者，始奏以文，復亂以武。

translations.literal: Zixia replied: "Ancient music begins its performance with civility and returns to disorder with martial vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Zixia replied: "Ancient music begins with civility and returns with martial vigor.

sentences.zh: 修身及家，平均天下。

translations.literal: It cultivates the person and extends to the family, and brings equity to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It cultivates the person and the family and brings equity to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 鄭衛之音者，奸聲以亂，溺而不止，優雜子女，不知父子。

translations.literal: The sounds of Zheng and Wei are corrupt sounds in disorder, drowning without end, mixing actors and women so that father and son are not known.
translations.idiomatic: The sounds of Zheng and Wei are corrupt sounds in disorder, drowning without end, mixing actors and women until father and son are not known.

sentences.zh: 今君所問者，樂也，所愛者，音也。

translations.literal: Now what my lord asks about is music; what he loves is mere sound.
translations.idiomatic: Now what my lord asks about is music; what he loves is mere sound.

sentences.zh: 夫樂之與音，相近而不同。

translations.literal: Music and sound are close yet not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Music and sound are close yet not the same.

sentences.zh: 為人君者，謹審其好惡。

translations.literal: For one who is ruler, carefully examine what one favors and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: For a ruler, carefully examine what he favors and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 」案聖人之作樂也，非止苟悅耳目而已矣。

translations.literal: For in the sages' making of music, it was not merely to please ears and eyes in passing.
translations.idiomatic: For in the sages' making of music, it was not merely to please ears and eyes in passing.

sentences.zh: 欲使在宗廟之內，君臣同聽之，則莫不和敬；

translations.literal: They wished that within the ancestral temple, when ruler and ministers listened together, none would fail to be harmonious and reverent;
translations.idiomatic: They wished that within the ancestral temple, when ruler and ministers listened together, all would be harmonious and reverent;

sentences.zh: 在鄉里之內，長幼同聽之，則莫不和順；

translations.literal: Within the districts, when old and young listen together, none fail to be harmonious;
translations.idiomatic: In the villages, when elders and youths listen as one, none fail to live in harmony;

sentences.zh: 在閨門之內，父子同聽之，則莫不和親。

translations.literal: Within the inner quarters, when father and son listen together, none fail to be close in kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Within the household gates, when father and son listen as one, none fail to be bound in affection.

sentences.zh: 此先王立樂之方也。

translations.literal: This is the method by which the former kings established music.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the way the ancient kings set music in the world.

sentences.zh: 故知聲而不知音者，禽獸是也；

translations.literal: Thus those who know sound but not tone are like beasts;
translations.idiomatic: Those who know sound but not pitch are no better than beasts;

sentences.zh: 知音而不知樂者，眾庶是也。

translations.literal: those who know tone but not music are like the common multitude.
translations.idiomatic: those who know pitch but not music are the common crowd.

sentences.zh: 故黃鐘、大呂，弦歌幹戚，童子皆能舞之。

translations.literal: Thus with the yellow bell and great bell, string songs, shields and axes, even children can dance to them.
translations.idiomatic: With the yellow bell and great bell, with strings and song, shields and halberds—even children can dance to them.

sentences.zh: 能知樂者，其惟君子。

translations.literal: Only the gentleman can know music.
translations.idiomatic: To know music—that belongs to the gentleman alone.

sentences.zh: 不知聲者不可與言音，不知音者不可與言樂，知樂則幾於道矣。

translations.literal: One who does not know sound cannot be spoken to about tone; one who does not know tone cannot be spoken to about music; to know music is to be near the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Speak not of pitch to one who knows not sound; speak not of music to one who knows not pitch; to know music is to stand almost upon the Way.

sentences.zh: 紂為無道，太師抱樂器以奔周。

translations.literal: Chou was without the Way, and the Grand Music Master embraced his instruments and fled to Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Chou walked without the Way; the Grand Music Master clasped his instruments and fled to the house of Chou.

sentences.zh: 晉君德薄，師曠固惜清徵。

translations.literal: The Chin ruler's virtue was thin, and Music Master Kuang still cherished the clear chih mode.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chin ruler's virtue ran thin, Music Master Kuang still would not lightly yield the clear chih mode.

sentences.zh: 上古之時，未有音樂，鼓腹擊壤，樂在其間。

translations.literal: In high antiquity there was as yet no music; beating the belly and striking the clod, joy lay among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the farthest antiquity there was no music yet—men beat their bellies and struck the earth, and joy lived in that alone.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「先王作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "The former kings made music to exalt virtue; in the Yin season they presented offerings to the Supreme Lord, to match the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "The former kings made music to exalt virtue; in the Yin season they offered to the Supreme Lord, pairing him with the ancestors."

sentences.zh: 」至於黃帝作《咸池》，顓頊作《六莖》，帝嚳作《五英》，堯作《大章》，舜作《大韶》，禹作《大夏》，湯作《大濩》，武王作《大武》。

translations.literal: As for the Yellow Emperor, he made the "Xian-ch'ih"; Chuan-hsü made the "Liu-stem"; Emperor Ku made the "Five Blossoms"; Yao made the "Great Pattern"; Shun made the "Great Shao"; Yü made the "Great Hsia"; T'ang made the "Great Hu"; King Wu made the "Great Martial."
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor composed the "Xian-ch'ih"; Chuan-hsü the "Six Stems"; Emperor Ku the "Five Blossoms"; Yao the "Great Pattern"; Shun the "Great Shao"; Yü the "Great Hsia"; T'ang the "Great Hu"; King Wu the "Great Martial."

sentences.zh: 從夏以來，年代久遠，唯有名字，其聲不可得聞。

translations.literal: From the Hsia onward the ages have been long; only the names remain, and their sounds cannot be heard.
translations.idiomatic: From the Hsia onward the years stretch too far; only the titles survive—their music cannot be heard.

sentences.zh: 自殷至周，備於《詩· 頌》。

translations.literal: From the Yin through the Chou, all is preserved in the Odes and Hymns.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yin through the Chou, the canon is complete in the Odes and Hymns.

sentences.zh: 故自聖賢已下，多習樂者，至如伏羲減瑟，文王足琴，仲尼擊磬，子路鼓瑟，漢高擊築，元帝吹簫。

translations.literal: Thus from the sages and worthies downward, many practiced music—for example Fu-hsi reduced the se, King Wen trimmed the ch'in, Chung-ni struck the ch'ing, Tzu-lu plucked the se, Han Kao-tsu beat the chu, and Yuan-ti played the hsiao.
translations.idiomatic: From the sages downward, many mastered music: Fu-hsi reduced the se, King Wen trimmed the ch'in, Chung-ni struck the stone chimes, Tzu-lu plucked the se, Han Kao-tsu beat the chu, and Yuan-ti played the hsiao.

sentences.zh: 漢祖之初，叔孫通因秦樂人，制宗廟之樂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Han house, Shusun T'ung, relying on Ch'in musicians, devised the music of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the first days of the Han, Shusun T'ung drew on Ch'in musicians and fashioned the ancestral-temple rites.

sentences.zh: 迎神於廟門，奏《嘉至之樂》，猶古降神之樂也。

translations.literal: To welcome the spirit at the temple gate, they played the music "Chia-chih," as in the ancient music for descending the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: At the temple gate they played "Chia-chih" to welcome the spirit—music of the old rite for summoning the god down.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入廟門，奏《永至之樂》，以為行步之節，猶古《采薺肆夏》也。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the temple gate, they played "Yung-chih," taking it as the measure for his steps, as in the ancient "Ts'ai-ch'i" and "Ssu-hsia."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor crossed the temple threshold, "Yung-chih" marked his pace—as once "Ts'ai-ch'i" and "Ssu-hsia" had done.

sentences.zh: 乾豆上薦，奏《登歌之樂》，猶古清廟之歌也。

translations.literal: When the dried offerings were set forth, they played the "Ascent Hymn," as in the ancient hymn of the pure temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the dried meats were raised in offering, they sang the Ascent Hymn—the old song of the pure temple.

sentences.zh: 登歌再終，奏《休成之樂》，美神饗也。

translations.literal: When the ascent hymn had been sung twice through, they played "Hsiu-ch'eng," praising the spirit's partaking.
translations.idiomatic: After the ascent hymn sounded twice, "Hsiu-ch'eng" followed, praising the god who had feasted.

sentences.zh: 皇帝就東廂坐定，奏《永安之樂》，美禮成也。

translations.literal: When the emperor took his seat in the east wing, they played "Yung-an," praising the completion of the rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sat in the east wing, "Yung-an" celebrated that the rite was complete.

sentences.zh: 其《休成》、《永至》二曲，叔孫通所制也。

translations.literal: The two pieces "Hsiu-ch'eng" and "Yung-chih" were composed by Shusun T'ung.
translations.idiomatic: The two airs "Hsiu-ch'eng" and "Yung-chih" were Shusun T'ung's own work.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖廟，奏《武德》、《文始》、《五行之舞》。

translations.literal: At the temple of Han Kao-tsu they performed the dances "Martial Virtue," "Literary Beginning," and "Five Phases."
translations.idiomatic: In Han Kao-tsu's temple they danced "Martial Virtue," "Literary Beginning," and the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 當春秋時，陳公子完奔齊，陳是舜後，故齊有《韶》樂。

translations.literal: In the time of the Spring and Autumn, the Ch'en noble Wan fled to Ch'i; Ch'en was descended from Shun, and therefore Ch'i possessed the Shao music.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn era, Wan of Ch'en fled to Ch'i; Ch'en was Shun's line, and so Ch'i kept the Shao.

sentences.zh: 孔子在齊聞韶，三月不知肉味是也。

translations.literal: When Confucius heard the Shao in Ch'i and for three months did not know the taste of meat—it was this.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius heard the Shao in Ch'i and for three months forgot the taste of meat—this is that story.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇滅齊，《韶》樂傳于秦。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor destroyed Ch'i, the Shao music passed to Ch'in.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor overthrew Ch'i, and the Shao passed into Ch'in.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖滅秦，《韶》樂傳於漢。

translations.literal: When Han Kao-tsu destroyed Ch'in, the Shao music passed to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kao-tsu overthrew Ch'in, and the Shao passed into Han.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖改名《文始》，以示不相襲也。

translations.literal: Han Kao-tsu renamed it "Literary Beginning," to show that he did not usurp the name.
translations.idiomatic: Han Kao-tsu renamed it "Literary Beginning," declaring he would not inherit the old title unchanged.

sentences.zh: 《五行舞》者，本周《大武》樂也，始皇改曰《五行》。

translations.literal: The "Five Phases" dance was originally the Chou "Great Martial" music; the First Emperor changed its name to "Five Phases."
translations.idiomatic: The Five Phases dance was once the Chou Great Martial; the First Emperor retitled it Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 及于孝文，復作《四時之舞》，以示天下安和，四時順也。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hsiao-wen they again made the "Four Seasons" dance, to show that all under Heaven was at peace and the four seasons in order.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hsiao-wen they added the Four Seasons dance, proclaiming peace under Heaven and the seasons in their course.

sentences.zh: 孝景采《武德舞》以為《昭德》，孝宣又采《昭德》以為《盛德》。

translations.literal: Hsiao-ching took the "Martial Virtue" dance and made it "Manifest Virtue"; Hsiao-hsüan again took "Manifest Virtue" and made it "Abundant Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Hsiao-ching drew on Martial Virtue to fashion Manifest Virtue; Hsiao-hsüan drew on Manifest Virtue to fashion Abundant Virtue.

sentences.zh: 雖變其名，大抵皆因秦舊事。

translations.literal: Though the names changed, for the most part all followed Ch'in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Names shifted, yet nearly everything still followed Ch'in custom.

sentences.zh: 至於晉、魏，皆用古樂。

translations.literal: As for Chin and Wei, both used the ancient music.
translations.idiomatic: In Chin and Wei alike, the court kept the ancient music.

sentences.zh: 魏之三祖，並制樂辭。

translations.literal: The three founders of Wei all composed lyrics for music.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's three founding emperors each wrote texts for the rites of sound.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉播越，五都傾蕩，樂聲南度，以是大備江東。

translations.literal: From the Yung-chia turmoil onward the five capitals were overthrown, and musical sounds passed south—therefore the eastern lands came to possess them in full.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yung-chia upheaval the five capitals fell, and music fled south—so the eastern riverlands came to hold the full tradition.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊已來，至於梁代，所行樂事，猶皆傳古。

translations.literal: From Sung and Ch'i down to the Liang, the music performed still all transmitted the ancient.
translations.idiomatic: From Sung and Ch'i through Liang, what the court played still came down from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 三雍四始，實稱大盛。

translations.literal: The three Yung and four Beginnings truly may be called a great flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The three Yung and four Beginnings—there was indeed a great flowering.

sentences.zh: 及侯景篡逆，樂師分散，其四舞三調，悉度偽齊。

translations.literal: When Hou Ching usurped and rebelled, music masters were scattered; the four dances and three modes all passed to the false Ch'i.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ching's treason scattered the masters; the four dances and three modes all crossed to false Ch'i.

sentences.zh: 齊氏雖知傳受，得曲而不用之於宗廟朝廷也。

translations.literal: Though the Ch'i house knew how to transmit and receive them, having the pieces they did not use them in the ancestral temple or at court.
translations.idiomatic: Ch'i could hand the tunes down, yet though they held the scores they never sounded them in temple or hall.

sentences.zh: 臣少好音律，留意管弦，年雖耆老，頗皆記憶。

translations.literal: Your servant from youth loved pitch and mode, attending to strings and pipes; though years have brought old age, I remember much.
translations.idiomatic: I have loved pitch and mode since youth and kept watch over strings and pipes; though I am old now, much still lives in memory.

sentences.zh: 及東土克定，樂人悉反，問其逗留，果雲是梁人所教。

translations.literal: When the eastern lands were pacified, musicians all returned; asked where they had stayed, they truly said they had been taught by men of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the east was settled, the musicians came back; asked where they had lingered, they answered, as truth bore out, that men of Liang had taught them.

sentences.zh: 今三調四舞，並皆有手，雖不能精熟，亦頗具雅聲。

translations.literal: Today the three modes and four dances all have living masters; though they cannot be finely skilled, they still preserve an elegant sound.
translations.idiomatic: The three modes and four dances still have hands to play them; though mastery is thin, an elegant tone remains.

sentences.zh: 若令教習傳授，庶得流傳古樂。

translations.literal: If they were taught and the tradition handed on, one might yet preserve the ancient music.
translations.idiomatic: Let them be taught and passed on, and the ancient music might yet survive.

sentences.zh: 然後取其會歸，撮其指要，因循損益，更制嘉名，歌盛德於當今，傳雅正于來葉，豈不美歟。

translations.literal: Then gather their principles, extract their essentials, follow precedent in adding and subtracting, and make new honorable names—singing the age's virtue now, transmitting elegance to generations to come: would it not be beautiful?
translations.idiomatic: Then gather their principles, seize their essentials, adjust by precedent, and give new honorable names—praising today's virtue, sending elegance to ages yet unborn: would that not be fine?

sentences.zh: 謹具錄三調四舞曲名，又制歌辭如別。

translations.literal: I respectfully set down in full the names of the three modes and four dances, and have composed lyrics for them separately.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully record the names of the three modes and four dances, and have drafted lyrics for them apart.

sentences.zh: 其有聲曲流宕，不可以陳於殿庭者，亦悉附之於後。

translations.literal: Those melodies that flow too freely to be presented in the palace hall I also append at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Tunes too wandering for the palace hall I append at the end as well.

sentences.zh: 書奏，別敕太常，取妥節度。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, a separate edict charged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to have T'uo set the measures.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in; a separate edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to let T'uo regulate the measures.

sentences.zh: 於是作清、平、瑟三調聲，又作八佾《鞸》、《鐸》、《巾》、《拂》四舞。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made the sounds of the three modes Ch'ing, P'ing, and Se, and also made the four dances of the eight rows: "Pien," "Tuo," "Chin," and "Fu."
translations.idiomatic: He then fashioned the three modes Ch'ing, P'ing, and Se, and the four eight-row dances: Pien, Tuo, Chin, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 先是太常所傳宗廟雅樂，歷數十年，唯作大呂，廢黃鐘。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the temple music transmitted by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, for decades only the great lü was used and the yellow bell was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: For decades the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had played only the great lü in temple music and cast aside the yellow bell.

sentences.zh: 妥又深乖古意，乃奏請用黃鐘。

translations.literal: T'uo again deeply departed from ancient meaning, and memorialized requesting use of the yellow bell.
translations.idiomatic: T'uo, finding this again far from antiquity, memorialized to restore the yellow bell.

sentences.zh: 詔下公卿議，從之。

translations.literal: An edict was sent down for discussion among the dukes and ministers, and they followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The edict went to the ministers for debate, and they assented.

sentences.zh: 俄而子蔚為秘書郎。

translations.literal: Before long Tzu-wei became Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Tzu-wei was made Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 有罪當刑，上哀之，減死論。

translations.literal: He had committed a crime deserving punishment; the emperor pitied him and reduced the sentence from death.
translations.idiomatic: He had earned a capital sentence; the emperor pitied him and spared his life.

sentences.zh: 是後恩禮漸薄。

translations.literal: After this favor and ceremony gradually grew thin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter imperial favor thinned by degrees.

sentences.zh: 六年，出為龍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he went out as governor of Lung-chou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was sent out as governor of Lung-chou.

sentences.zh: 時有負笈遊學者，妥皆為講說教授之。

translations.literal: Whenever students came bearing their bundles to study abroad, T'uo lectured and taught them all.
translations.idiomatic: Students who came with book-bundles to study he lectured and taught without stint.

sentences.zh: 又為《刺史箴》，勒於州門外。

translations.literal: He also composed an "Admonition for Governors" and had it carved outside the prefectural gate.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote an Admonition for Governors and had it cut into stone at the prefectural gate.

sentences.zh: 在職三年，以疾請還，詔許之。

translations.literal: After three years in office he asked to return on account of illness, and an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he begged leave for illness; the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 復知學事。

translations.literal: He again took charge of academic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again oversaw the schools.

sentences.zh: 時上方使蘇夔在太常參議鐘律，夔有所建議，朝士多從之。

translations.literal: At that time the court had sent Su Kuei to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliberate on bells and pitch; Kuei made proposals, and many court gentlemen followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court had posted Su Kuei at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to debate bells and pitch; many officials sided with his proposals.

sentences.zh: 妥獨不同，每言夔之短。

translations.literal: T'uo alone disagreed and constantly spoke of Kuei's faults.
translations.idiomatic: T'uo alone dissented, and at every turn spoke of Kuei's shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 帝下其議，群臣多排妥。

translations.literal: The emperor sent down their deliberations, and most of the ministers rejected T'uo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor circulated their debate; most ministers turned against T'uo.

sentences.zh: 妥復上封事，指陳得失，大抵論時政損益，並指斥當世朋黨。

translations.literal: T'uo again submitted a sealed memorial, pointing out gains and losses; for the most part he discussed improvements and harms in current policy, and also denounced the factionalism of the age.
translations.idiomatic: T'uo sent up another sealed memorial on gains and losses—mostly on the state of policy, and on the cliques of the day.

sentences.zh: 於是蘇威及吏部尚書盧愷、侍郎薛道衡等皆坐得罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su Wei, Minister of Personnel Lu K'ai, Vice Director Hsüeh Tao-heng, and others all suffered punishment for their offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Minister of Personnel Lu K'ai, Vice Director Hsüeh Tao-heng, and others were all punished in the affair.

sentences.zh: 除伊州刺史，不行。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of I-chou but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was named governor of I-chou but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 尋為國子祭酒，卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he became Director of the National University and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Director of the National University and died in that office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Su.

sentences.zh: 撰《周易講疏》三卷、《孝經義疏》二卷、《莊子義疏》四卷。

translations.literal: He authored Expository Commentary on the Changes in three juan, Expository Commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety in two juan, and Expository Commentary on Chuang-tzu in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Expository Commentary on the Changes in three juan, on the Classic of Filial Piety in two, and on Chuang-tzu in four.

sentences.zh: 與沈重等撰《三十六科鬼神感應等大義》九卷、《封禪書》一卷、《樂要》一卷、文集十卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: Together with Shen Chung and others he compiled Great Principles on the Thirty-six Categories of Spirit Response and the Like in nine juan, a book on the Feng and Shan sacrifices in one juan, Essentials of Music in one juan, and collected writings in ten juan—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: With Shen Chung and others he compiled Great Principles on Spirit Response in nine juan, a book on the Feng and Shan in one, Essentials of Music in one, and ten juan of collected writings—all in circulation.

sentences.zh: 于時學士之自江南來者，蕭該、包愷並知名。

translations.literal: At that time among scholars who had come from south of the Yangtze, Hsiao Gai and Pao K'ai were both renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Among scholars who had come from the south, Hsiao Gai and Pao K'ai were both famed.

sentences.zh: 蕭該，蘭陵人。

translations.literal: Hsiao Gai was a man of Lan-ling.
translations.idiomatic: Hsiao Gai came from Lan-ling.

sentences.zh: 梁鄱陽王恢之孫，少封攸侯。

translations.literal: He was grandson of the Liang Prince of P'o-yang, Hui; in youth he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was grandson of the Liang Prince of P'o-yang, Hui, and in youth held the marquisate of Yu.

sentences.zh: 荊州平，與何妥同至長安。

translations.literal: When Ching-chou was pacified, he came to Ch'ang-an together with He T'o.
translations.idiomatic: When Ching-chou fell, he reached Ch'ang-an with He T'o.

sentences.zh: 性篤學，《詩》、《書》、《春秋》、《禮記》並通大義，尤精《漢書》，甚為貴遊所禮。

translations.literal: By nature he was devoted to learning; the Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn, and Record of Rites he all mastered in their great principles, and he was especially expert in the Han shu—greatly honored by the noble and powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to learning by nature, he mastered the broad sense of the Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn, and Record of Rites, and excelled above all in the Han shu—men of rank held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，賜爵山陰縣公，拜國子博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of K'ai-huang he was granted the title Duke of Shan-yin county and appointed Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In early K'ai-huang he was made Duke of Shan-yin and Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 奉詔與妥正定經史。

translations.literal: By imperial command he joined T'o in fixing the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he worked with T'o to fix the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 然各執所見，遞相是非，久而不能就。

translations.literal: Yet each clung to his own view and criticized the other in turn; after a long time they could not finish.
translations.idiomatic: Each held to his own view and refuted the other; months passed and nothing was settled.

sentences.zh: 上譴而罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked them and dismissed the project.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproved them and called the work off.

sentences.zh: 該後撰《漢書》及《文選音義》，咸為當時所貴。

translations.literal: Later Gai compiled phonological studies on the Han shu and the Wen hsüan, both prized in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Gai later wrote phonological studies on the Han shu and the Wen hsüan—both were treasures of the time.

sentences.zh: 包愷，字和樂，東海人。

translations.literal: Pao K'ai, styled Ho-lo, was a man of Tung-hai.
translations.idiomatic: Pao K'ai, styled Ho-lo, came from Tung-hai.

sentences.zh: 其兄愉，明《五經》，愷悉傳其業。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yu was accomplished in the Five Classics; K'ai fully inherited his learning.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yu mastered the Five Classics; K'ai took all his teaching.

sentences.zh: 及從王仲通受《史記》、《漢書》，尤稱精究。

translations.literal: He also studied the Shih chi and Han shu under Wang Chung-t'ung, and was especially praised for thorough mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Chung-t'ung he studied the Records of the Historian and the Han shu, and was famed for depth.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為國子助教。

translations.literal: In the Ta-yeh era he served as Assistant Instructor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ta-yeh reign he was Assistant Instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 於是《漢書》學者以蕭、包二人為宗，遠近聚徒教授者數千人。

translations.literal: Thereupon students of the Han shu took the two men, Hsiao and Pao, as their masters; from near and far those who gathered disciples to teach numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Han shu made Hsiao and Pao their patriarchs; thousands came from far and near to sit at their feet.

sentences.zh: 卒，門人起墳立碣焉。

translations.literal: When he died, his disciples raised his tomb and set up a stele.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his disciples raised his mound and carved a stele.

sentences.zh: 房暉遠，字崇儒，恆山真定人也。

translations.literal: Fang Hui-yüan, styled Ch'ung-ju, was a man of Chen-ting in Heng-shan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Hui-yüan, styled Ch'ung-ju, came from Chen-ting in Heng-shan.

sentences.zh: 世傳儒學。

translations.literal: His family for generations transmitted Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian learning ran in his house for generations.

sentences.zh: 暉遠幼有志行，明《三禮》、《春秋三傳》、《詩》、《書》、《周易》，兼善圖緯。

translations.literal: From youth Hui-yüan had purpose and conduct; he was accomplished in the Three Rites, the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn, the Odes, Documents, and Changes, and was also skilled in charts and weft texts.
translations.idiomatic: Hui-yüan was purposeful from boyhood, versed in the Three Rites, the three Spring and Autumn commentaries, the Odes, Documents, and Changes, and skilled besides in charts and apocrypha.

sentences.zh: 恆以教授為務，遠方負笈而從者，動以千計。

translations.literal: He constantly made instruction his task; those who came from afar bearing bundles to follow him often numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching was his constant work; disciples who came from afar with book-bundles often numbered a thousand or more.

sentences.zh: 齊南陽王綽為定州刺史，聞其名，召為博士。

translations.literal: When the Ch'i Prince of Nan-yang, Ch'uo, was governor of Ting-chou, hearing his name he summoned him as Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: The Ch'i Prince of Nan-yang, Ch'uo, governor of Ting-chou, heard of him and made him Erudite.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，搜訪儒俊，暉遠首應辟命，授小學下士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chou pacified Ch'i he sought out Confucian worthies; Hui-yüan was first to answer the summons and was appointed Junior Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou Wu-ti pacified Ch'i he sought Confucian talent; Hui-yüan was first to answer and was made Junior Scholar.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: When Sui Wen-ti received the abdication, he was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen-ti took the throne, Hui-yüan became Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 太常卿牛弘每稱為《五經》庫。

translations.literal: Director Niu Hung of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices often called him a storehouse of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hung, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, called him a storehouse of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書韋世康薦之，遷太學博士。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wei Shih-k'ang recommended him, and he was transferred to Erudite of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shih-k'ang of Personnel recommended him, and he rose to Erudite of the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 尋與沛公鄭譯修正樂章。

translations.literal: Before long he joined the Duke of P'ei, Cheng I, in correcting the ritual hymns.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined the Duke of P'ei, Cheng I, in revising the ritual hymns.

sentences.zh: 後復為太常博士，未幾擢為國子博士。

translations.literal: Later he again became Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; before long he was promoted to Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then was soon raised to Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 會上令國子生通一經者，並悉薦舉，將擢用之。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor ordered that all National University students who had mastered one classic were to be recommended and would be promoted for employment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered every National University student who had mastered one classic to be recommended for office.

sentences.zh: 既策問訖，博士不能時定臧否。

translations.literal: After the policy examination was finished, the Erudites could not promptly decide who passed and who failed.
translations.idiomatic: When the examination ended, the Erudites could not settle who had passed.

sentences.zh: 祭酒元善怪問之，暉遠曰：「江南、河北，義例不同，博士不能遍涉。

translations.literal: Director of Studies Yüan Shan, wondering, asked him; Hui-yüan said: "Between south of the Yangtze and north of the Yellow River, the patterns of interpretation differ, and the Erudites cannot cover them all.
translations.idiomatic: Director Yüan Shan asked why; Hui-yüan said, "South of the Yangtze and north of the river the exegetical traditions differ—the Erudites cannot master them all.

sentences.zh: 學生皆持其所短，稱己所長；

translations.literal: The students all hold to what others lack and praise what they themselves excel in;
translations.idiomatic: Each student clings to another's weakness and praises his own strength;

sentences.zh: 博士各各自疑，所以久而不決也。

translations.literal: the Erudites each doubt themselves, and therefore for long they could not decide."
translations.idiomatic: the Erudites doubt themselves in turn—hence the long delay."

sentences.zh: 」祭酒因令暉遠考定之，暉遠攬筆便下，初無疑滯。

translations.literal: The Director thereupon had Hui-yüan examine and decide; Hui-yüan took up the brush and wrote his judgments at once, without hesitation from the start.
translations.idiomatic: The Director set Hui-yüan to judge; he took brush and wrote at once, never faltering.

sentences.zh: 或有不服者，暉遠問其所傳義疏，輒為始末誦之，然後出其所短。

translations.literal: If any were not satisfied, Hui-yüan asked what commentary they transmitted and at once recited it from beginning to end, then pointed out their shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: When a man demurred, Hui-yüan asked which commentary he followed, recited it through from end to end, then named his faults.

sentences.zh: 自是無敢飾非者。

translations.literal: From this none dared conceal their errors.
translations.idiomatic: After that none dared hide his failings.

sentences.zh: 所試四五百人，數日便決。

translations.literal: Of the four or five hundred examined, he decided within a few days.
translations.idiomatic: Four or five hundred candidates—he settled them in a few days.

sentences.zh: 諸儒莫不推其通博，皆自以為不能測也。

translations.literal: The Confucians all praised his comprehensive learning; each felt he could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Every scholar praised his breadth; each felt he could not plumb his depth.

sentences.zh: 尋奉詔預修令式。

translations.literal: Before long he received command to take part in compiling statutes and forms.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to help compile statutes and forms.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗謂群臣曰：「自古天子有女樂乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once said to the assembled ministers: "From antiquity, did Son of Heaven ever have female musicians?"
translations.idiomatic: Wen-ti once asked the ministers, "Since antiquity, has any Son of Heaven kept female musicians?"

sentences.zh: 」楊素以下，莫知所出，遂言無女樂。

translations.literal: Below Yang Su, none knew the source, and they thereupon said there were no female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: From Yang Su downward, none knew the allusion, and they said there were none.

sentences.zh: 暉遠曰：「臣聞'窈窕淑女，鐘鼓樂之'，此即王者房中之樂，著於《雅》《頌》，不得言無。

translations.literal: Hui-yüan said: "I have heard, 'Fair and gentle maiden—bells and drums rejoice in her'—this is the Son of Heaven's chamber music, set forth in the Ya and Sung; one cannot say there were none."
translations.idiomatic: Hui-yüan said, "I have heard, 'Fair and gentle maiden—bells and drums rejoice in her.' That is the king's chamber music, recorded in the Ya and Sung—it cannot be called absent."

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，卒官，朝廷嗟惜焉，賵賻甚厚，贈員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Jen-shou era he died in office; the court sighed in regret, the funeral gifts were very generous, and he was posthumously made Supernumerary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Jen-shou he died in office; the court mourned him, gave lavish funeral gifts, and posthumously made him Supernumerary Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 馬光，字榮伯，武安人也。

translations.literal: Ma Kuang, styled Jung-po, was a man of Wu-an.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Kuang, styled Jung-po, came from Wu-an.

sentences.zh: 少好學，從師數十年，晝夜不息，圖書讖緯，莫不畢覽。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; he followed teachers for decades, day and night without rest, and of books, charts, and weft texts there was none he did not read through.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved learning; for decades he followed teachers without rest by day or night, and read every book, chart, and apocryphon he could find.

sentences.zh: 尤明《三禮》，為儒者所宗。

translations.literal: He was especially accomplished in the Three Rites and was honored by the Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled above all in the Three Rites, and the ru looked to him.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，征山東義學之士，光與張仲讓、孔籠、竇仕榮、張買奴、劉祖仁等俱至，並授太學博士，時人號為六儒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui K'ai-huang, righteous scholars of the eastern mountains were summoned; Kuang, together with Chang Chung-jang, K'ung Lung, Tou Shih-jung, Chang Mai-nu, Liu Tsu-jen, and others all arrived, and were appointed Erudites of the Grand Academy—the men of the time called them the Six Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: In early K'ai-huang the court summoned righteous scholars of the east; Kuang came with Chang Chung-jang, K'ung Lung, Tou Shih-jung, Chang Mai-nu, Liu Tsu-jen, and others, all made Erudites of the Grand Academy—the age called them the Six Confucians.

sentences.zh: 然皆鄙野無儀範，朝廷不之貴也。

translations.literal: Yet all were rustic and without decorum, and the court did not esteem them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were coarse and without manners, and the court held them cheap.

sentences.zh: 仕榮尋病死。

translations.literal: Shih-jung soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shih-jung soon died.

sentences.zh: 仲讓未幾告歸鄉里，著書十卷，自云：「此書若奏，必為宰相。

translations.literal: Chung-jang before long asked leave to return to his native place and authored ten juan of writings, saying himself: "If this book is submitted, I shall surely become chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Chung-jang soon went home and wrote ten juan, saying, "If this book reaches the throne, I shall surely be chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」又數言玄象事。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly spoke of celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke often of omens in the sky.

sentences.zh: 州縣列上，竟坐誅。

translations.literal: The prefecture and county reported upward, and in the end he was put to death for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: The local officials reported him, and in the end he was executed.

sentences.zh: 孔籠、張買奴、劉祖仁未幾亦被譴亡。

translations.literal: K'ung Lung, Chang Mai-nu, and Liu Tsu-jen before long were also punished and perished.
translations.idiomatic: K'ung Lung, Chang Mai-nu, and Liu Tsu-jen soon shared the same fate.

sentences.zh: 唯光獨存。

translations.literal: Only Kuang alone survived.
translations.idiomatic: Only Kuang remained.

sentences.zh: 嘗因釋奠，帝親幸國子學，王公已下畢集，光升坐講《禮》，啟發章門。

translations.literal: Once, on the occasion of the libation sacrifice, the emperor personally visited the National University; kings, dukes, and all below gathered; Kuang ascended the seat and lectured on the Rites, opening and guiding the gates of meaning.
translations.idiomatic: At a libation rite the emperor visited the National University; lords and officials gathered; Kuang mounted the dais and lectured on the Rites, opening the gates of meaning.

sentences.zh: 已而諸儒生以次論難者十餘，皆當時碩學。

translations.literal: Then more than ten Confucian students in turn raised objections for debate—all were leading scholars of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Then a dozen leading scholars rose in turn to debate him.

sentences.zh: 光剖析疑滯，雖辭非俊辯，而《禮》義弘贍。

translations.literal: Kuang analyzed what was doubtful and obstructed; though his words were not brilliantly eloquent, the meaning of the Rites was broad and ample.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang untied every knot; his words were not sharp, yet the Rites stood wide and full before them.

sentences.zh: 論者莫測其淺深，咸共推服。

translations.literal: The debaters could not measure his depth or shallowness, and all together submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: None could tell shallow from deep; all yielded.

sentences.zh: 上嘉而勞焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 山東《三禮》學者，自熊安生後，唯宗光一人。

translations.literal: Among scholars of the Three Rites in the eastern mountains, after Hsiung An-sheng only Kuang alone was honored as master.
translations.idiomatic: After Hsiung An-sheng, only Kuang was master to the east for the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 初教授瀛、博間，門徒千數，至是多負笈從入長安。

translations.literal: At first he taught between Ying and Po, with disciples in the thousands; by then many came bearing bundles to follow him into Ch'ang-an.
translations.idiomatic: He had taught between Ying and Po with a thousand disciples; now many followed him into Ch'ang-an with book-bundles on their backs.

sentences.zh: 後數年，丁母憂歸鄉里，以疾卒於家。

translations.literal: Some years later he returned to his native place in mourning for his mother and died of illness at home.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he went home for his mother's mourning and died there of illness.

sentences.zh: 劉焯，字士元，信都昌亭人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ch'ao, styled Shih-yüan, was a man of Ch'ang-t'ing in Hsin-tu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ch'ao, styled Shih-yüan, came from Ch'ang-t'ing in Hsin-tu.

sentences.zh: 犀額龜背，望高視遠，聰敏沉深，弱不好弄。

translations.literal: Rhino brow and tortoise back, gaze lofty and sight far, clever and keen, deep and reserved—from weakness he did not care for play.
translations.idiomatic: He had a rhinoceros brow and tortoise back, a far-reaching gaze, a clever and deep mind, and from childhood scorned idle play.

sentences.zh: 少與河間劉炫結盟為友，同受《詩》于同郡劉軌思，受《左傳》于廣平郭懋，嘗問《禮》于阜城熊安生，皆不卒業而去。

translations.literal: In youth he formed a bond of friendship with Liu Hsüan of Ho-chien; together they received the Odes from Liu Kuei-ssu of the same commandery, the Tso chuan from Kuo Mao of Kuang-p'ing, and once asked about the Rites of Hsiung An-sheng of Fu-ch'eng—all left without completing their studies.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he swore friendship with Liu Hsüan of Ho-chien; both studied the Odes under Liu Kuei-ssu, the Tso chuan under Kuo Mao of Kuang-p'ing, and once questioned Hsiung An-sheng on the Rites—yet left each master before finishing.

sentences.zh: 武強交津橋劉智海家，素多墳籍，焯就之讀書，向經十載，雖衣食不繼，晏如也。

translations.literal: At the home of Liu Chih-hai of Chiao-chin Bridge in Wu-ch'iang, where tombs and records abounded from of old, Ch'ao went to read; for nearly ten years, though food and clothing failed in succession, he was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He read for nearly ten years at the house of Liu Chih-hai by Chiao-chin Bridge in Wu-ch'iang, where old tomes piled high—though food and clothes often failed, he was content.

sentences.zh: 遂以儒學知名，為州博士。

translations.literal: Thereupon he became renowned for Confucian learning and was made Erudite of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He won fame as a Confucian and became the prefectural Erudite.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，刺史趙煚引為從事。

translations.literal: In the K'ai-huang era of Sui, Governor Chao Huan of the province summoned him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui K'ai-huang, Governor Chao Huan took him on as aide.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，射策甲科。

translations.literal: He was recommended as hsiu-ts'ai and in the target-shooting examination placed in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as hsiu-ts'ai, he placed first in the policy examination.
