sentences.zh: 與著作郎王劭同修國史，兼參議律曆。

translations.literal: Together with Academician Wang Shao he revised the national history and also took part in deliberating on law and calendar.
translations.idiomatic: With Academician Wang Shao he revised the national history and joined debates on law and calendar.

sentences.zh: 仍直門下省，以待顧問。

translations.literal: He continued on duty at the Department of the Imperial Secretariat, awaiting consultation.
translations.idiomatic: He served at the Imperial Secretariat, awaiting the emperor's questions.

sentences.zh: 俄除員外將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Supernumerary General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Supernumerary General.

sentences.zh: 後與諸儒于秘書省考定群言。

translations.literal: Later, with the various Confucians, he examined and fixed the various writings in the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined other scholars in the Imperial Library to fix the canon of texts.

sentences.zh: 因假還鄉里，縣令韋之業引為功曹。

translations.literal: On leave he returned to his native place; Magistrate Wei Chih-yeh of the county summoned him as Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: On leave he went home; Magistrate Wei Chih-yeh made him Merit Officer.

sentences.zh: 尋復入京，與左僕射楊素、吏部尚書牛弘、國子祭酒蘇威、元善、博士蕭該、何妥、太學博士房暉遠、崔崇德、晉王文學崔賾等，于國子共論古今滯義，前賢所不通者。

translations.literal: Before long he again entered the capital and, with Left Vice Director Yang Su, Minister of Personnel Niu Hung, Director of the National University Su Wei and Yüan Shan, Erudites Hsiao Gai, He T'o, Erudite of the Grand Academy Fang Hui-yüan, Ts'ui Ch'ung-te, Literary Companion to the Prince of Chin Ts'ui Yen, and others, at the National University debated obscure points of past and present that former worthies had not penetrated.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital and, with Yang Su, Niu Hung, Su Wei, Yüan Shan, Hsiao Gai, He T'o, Fang Hui-yüan, Ts'ui Ch'ung-te, Ts'ui Yen, and others, debated at the National University the hard knots of antiquity that sages had never cleared.

sentences.zh: 每升坐，論難鋒起，皆不能屈。

translations.literal: Whenever he took his seat, debate flared like spearpoints, and none could bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sat, debate flashed like blades, and none could bend him.

sentences.zh: 楊素等莫不服其精博。

translations.literal: Yang Su and the others all submitted to his profound learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su and the rest yielded to his depth.

sentences.zh: 六年，運洛陽《石經》至京師，文字磨滅，莫能知者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Lo-yang Stone Classics were transported to the capital; the characters were worn away and none could read them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Lo-yang Stone Classics reached the capital worn smooth—no one could read them.

sentences.zh: 奉敕與劉炫二人論義，深挫諸儒，咸懷妒恨。

translations.literal: By imperial command he and Liu Hsüan together expounded their meaning, deeply defeating the various Confucians, who all harbored jealous hatred.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he and Liu Hsüan expounded them, crushing the other scholars, who burned with envy.

sentences.zh: 遂為飛章所謗，除名。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was slandered by a flying memorial and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: A flying memorial slandered him, and he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 於是優遊鄉里，專以教授著述為務，孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wandered at ease in his native place, devoting himself solely to instruction and authorship, never weary.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered at ease at home, teaching and writing without rest.

sentences.zh: 賈、馬、王、鄭所傳章句，多所是非。

translations.literal: Of the commentarial traditions transmitted by Chia, Ma, Wang, and Cheng, he approved or rejected many.
translations.idiomatic: He challenged much in the commentaries handed down from Chia, Ma, Wang, and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 《九章算術》、《周髀》、《七曜曆書》十餘部，推步日月之經，量度山海之術，莫不核其根本，窮其秘奧。

translations.literal: Of more than ten works such as the Nine Chapters on Mathematical Art, the Chou pei, and the Seven Luminaries Calendar Book, the methods for calculating sun and moon and for measuring mountains and seas—none did he fail to examine at the root and exhaust in secret subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten works—the Nine Chapters, the Chou pei, the Seven Luminaries Calendar—methods for sun and moon, for mountains and seas: he traced every root and plumbed every secret.

sentences.zh: 著《稽極》十卷，《曆書》十卷，《五經述議》，並行於世。

translations.literal: He authored Investigations into the Ultimate in ten juan, a book on Calendrics in ten juan, and Discussions of the Five Classics—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Investigations into the Ultimate in ten juan, Calendrics in ten juan, and Discussions of the Five Classics—all in circulation.

sentences.zh: 劉炫聰明博學，名亞於焯，故時人稱二劉焉。

translations.literal: Liu Hsüan was clever and broadly learned; his fame was second to Ch'ao's, and therefore men of the time called them the Two Lius.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hsüan was clever and vast in learning, second only to Ch'ao—men called them the Two Lius.

sentences.zh: 天下名儒後進，質疑受業，不遠千里而至者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Famous Confucians and later students who came from afar bearing doubts to receive instruction, not hesitating to travel a thousand li, were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Famed scholars and young students came a thousand li with their doubts—no one could count them.

sentences.zh: 論者以為數百年已來，博學通儒無能出其右者。

translations.literal: Discussants held that for several hundred years there had been no broadly learned Confucian who could match him.
translations.idiomatic: For centuries, men said, no scholar of such breadth had appeared.

sentences.zh: 然懷抱不曠，又嗇於財。

translations.literal: Yet his breast was not broad, and he was stingy with wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his heart was narrow, and he clutched his coins.

sentences.zh: 不行束脩者，未嘗有所教誨，時人以此少之。

translations.literal: Those who did not present the bundle of dried meat he never instructed; for this the men of the time thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: He never taught a man who brought no bundle of dried meat; for that the age thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 廢主子勇聞而召之，未及進謁，詔令事蜀王。

translations.literal: The deposed heir apparent, Tzu-yung, heard of him and summoned him; before he could present himself at audience, an edict ordered him to serve the Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed heir Tzu-yung summoned him; before he could attend, an edict sent him to the Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 非共好也，久之不至。

translations.literal: They were not of like mind, and for long he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Their tempers did not match, and he delayed.

sentences.zh: 王聞而大怒，遣人枷送於蜀，配之軍防。

translations.literal: The prince heard and was greatly angry, and sent men to fetter him and escort him to Shu, assigning him to military guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: The prince raged, sent men to fetter him and drag him to Shu, and set him to guard the army.

sentences.zh: 其後典校書籍。

translations.literal: Afterward he was put in charge of collating books.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was charged with collating books.

sentences.zh: 王以罪廢，焯又與諸儒修定禮、律，除雲騎尉。

translations.literal: When the prince was deposed for his crime, Ch'ao again joined the various Confucians in revising and fixing the Rites and laws, and was made Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince fell, Ch'ao helped the scholars fix the Rites and laws and was made Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷太學博士，俄以品卑去職。

translations.literal: When Yang-ti acceded, he was transferred to Erudite of the Grand Academy; before long he left office because his rank was low.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yang-ti he became Erudite of the Grand Academy, then left because his rank was too low.

sentences.zh: 數年，復被征以待顧問。

translations.literal: Some years later he was again summoned to await consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was summoned again to await the emperor's questions.

sentences.zh: 因上所著《曆書》，與太史令張胄玄多不同，被駁不用。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted his authored book on Calendrics; it differed greatly from Grand Astrologer Chang Chou-hsüan and was rejected and not used.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted his Calendrics; it clashed with Grand Astrologer Chang Chou-hsüan and was rejected.

sentences.zh: 卒，劉炫為之請諡，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: When he died, Liu Hsüan requested a posthumous title for him, and the court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Liu Hsüan asked a posthumous name; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 劉炫，字光伯，河間景城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Hsüan, styled Kuang-po, was a man of Ching-ch'eng in Ho-chien.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hsüan, styled Kuang-po, came from Ching-ch'eng in Ho-chien.

sentences.zh: 少以聰敏見稱。

translations.literal: From youth he was praised for cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was famed for quickness of mind.

sentences.zh: 與信都劉焯閉戶讀書，十年不出。

translations.literal: Together with Liu Ch'ao of Hsin-tu he shut the door and read books, for ten years not going out.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Ch'ao of Hsin-tu he barred the door and read for ten years without stepping out.

sentences.zh: 炫眸子精明，視日不眩，強記默識，莫與為儔。

translations.literal: Hsüan's pupils were bright and clear; he could gaze at the sun without dazzle, and in strong memory and silent retention none could be his match.
translations.idiomatic: His eyes were bright—he could stare at the sun unblinded—and in memory none could match him.

sentences.zh: 左畫圓，右畫方，口誦，目數，耳聽，五事同舉，無所遺失。

translations.literal: With the left hand he drew a circle, with the right a square; he recited with the mouth, counted with the eyes, listened with the ears—five tasks raised together, nothing lost.
translations.idiomatic: Left hand a circle, right hand a square; mouth reciting, eyes counting, ears listening—five tasks at once, nothing dropped.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，瀛州刺史宇文亢召為戶曹從事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chou pacified Ch'i, the governor of Ying-chou, Yuwen K'ang, summoned him as Clerk of the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou Wu-ti pacified Ch'i, Ying-chou governor Yuwen K'ang made him Clerk of the Household Bureau.

sentences.zh: 後刺史李繪署禮曹從事，以吏幹知名。

translations.literal: Later Governor Li Hui of the province appointed him Clerk of the Rites Bureau, and he became known for administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Later Governor Li Hui made him Clerk of the Rites Bureau, famed for competence in office.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，奉敕與著作郎王劭同修國史，俄直門下省，以待顧問。

translations.literal: In the K'ai-huang era of Sui, by imperial command he joined Academician Wang Shao in revising the national history; before long he was on duty at the Imperial Secretariat, awaiting consultation.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui K'ai-huang he joined Wang Shao in revising the national history, then served at the Imperial Secretariat awaiting questions.

sentences.zh: 又詔諸術者修天文律曆，兼于內史省考定群言。

translations.literal: He was again ordered, with the various specialists, to revise astronomy, pitch, and calendar, and also to examine and fix the various writings in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Again he was ordered with specialists to revise astronomy, pitch, and calendar, and to fix texts at the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 內史令博陵李德林甚禮之。

translations.literal: Director Li Te-lin of Po-ling in the Imperial Secretariat greatly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te-lin, Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Po-ling, treated him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 炫雖遍直三省，竟不得官，為縣司責其賦役。

translations.literal: Though Hsüan served throughout the three departments, in the end he received no office, and the county office pressed him for tax and corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served all three departments, he won no post, and the county pressed him for tax and labor.

sentences.zh: 炫自陳于內史，內史送詣吏部。

translations.literal: Hsüan stated his case to the Imperial Secretariat, and the Secretariat sent him to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded his case to the Secretariat, which sent him on to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尚書韋世康問其所能，炫自為狀曰：「《周禮》、《禮記》、《毛詩》、《尚書》、《公羊》、《左傳》、《孝經》、《論語》，孔、鄭、王、何、服、杜等注，凡十三家，雖義有精粗，並堪講授；

translations.literal: Minister Wei Shih-k'ang asked what he could do; Hsüan wrote his own petition, saying: "The Rites of Chou, Record of Rites, Mao Odes, Documents, Kung-yang, Tso chuan, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects—the commentaries of Confucius, Cheng, Wang, Ho, Fu, and Tu, thirteen houses in all—though in meaning some are fine and some coarse, all can be lectured upon;
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wei Shih-k'ang asked his talents; Hsüan wrote: "The Rites of Chou, Record of Rites, Mao Odes, Documents, Kung-yang, Tso chuan, Filial Piety, and Analects—the commentaries of K'ung, Cheng, Wang, Ho, Fu, and Tu, thirteen houses in all, coarse or fine, I can lecture on them all;

sentences.zh: 《周易》、《儀禮》、《谷梁》用功差少；

translations.literal: the Changes, Ceremonies, and Ku-liang I have applied myself to somewhat less;
translations.idiomatic: the Changes, Ceremonies, and Ku-liang somewhat less;

sentences.zh: 史子文集，嘉言故事，咸誦於心；

translations.literal: histories, masters, and collected writings, fine words and old stories, I recite all by heart;
translations.idiomatic: histories, masters, anthologies—fine phrases and old tales I hold in memory;

sentences.zh: 天文、律曆，窮核微妙。

translations.literal: astronomy and pitch and calendar I have examined to their subtlest point."
translations.idiomatic: astronomy, pitch, and calendar I have traced to their subtlest point."

sentences.zh: 至於公私文翰，未嘗假手。

translations.literal: As for public and private documents, he never borrowed another's hand.
translations.idiomatic: For public or private writing he never borrowed another's hand.

sentences.zh: 」吏部竟不詳試。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel in the end did not examine him in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel never tested him at all.

sentences.zh: 然在朝知名之士十餘人，保明炫所陳不謬，於是除殿內將軍。

translations.literal: Yet more than ten renowned men at court attested that what Hsüan stated was not in error, and thereupon he was made Palace Interior General.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a dozen famed men at court vouched that his words were true, and he was made Palace Interior General.

sentences.zh: 時牛弘奏購求天下遺逸之書，炫遂偽造書百餘卷，題為《連山易》、《魯史記》等，錄上送官，取賞而去。

translations.literal: At that time Niu Hung memorialized to purchase lost books of the realm; Hsüan thereupon forged more than a hundred juan, titling them the Lien-shan Changes, Records of Lu, and the like, copied them and sent them to the office, took the reward, and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Niu Hung sought lost books of the realm, Hsüan forged more than a hundred juan—the Lien-shan Changes, Records of Lu, and the like—sent them in, took the reward, and fled.

sentences.zh: 後有人訟之，經赦免死，坐除名。

translations.literal: Later someone sued him; through an amnesty he escaped death but was punished by being struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Someone sued him; an amnesty spared his life, but he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 歸於家，以教授為務。

translations.literal: He returned home and made instruction his task.
translations.idiomatic: He went home and took up teaching.

sentences.zh: 廢太子勇聞而召之。

translations.literal: The deposed heir apparent, Yung, heard of him and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed heir Yung heard of him and summoned him.

sentences.zh: 既至京師，敕令事蜀王秀，遷延不往。

translations.literal: When he had reached the capital, an edict ordered him to serve Prince Hsiu of Shu, but he delayed and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the capital; an edict sent him to Prince Hsiu of Shu, but he lingered and would not go.

sentences.zh: 秀大怒，枷送益州。

translations.literal: Hsiu was greatly angry and sent him in the cangue to I-chou.
translations.idiomatic: Hsiu raged and sent him in the cangue to I-chou.

sentences.zh: 既而配為帳內，每使執仗為門衛。

translations.literal: Before long he was assigned within the curtain; each day he was made to hold weapons as gate guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned to the prince's household and made to stand at the gate with a spear.

sentences.zh: 俄而釋之，典校書史。

translations.literal: Before long he was released and put in charge of collating books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was freed and charged with collating books.

sentences.zh: 炫因擬屈原《卜居》為《筮塗》以自寄。

translations.literal: Hsüan thereupon modeled Ch'ü Yüan's "Divining" and made "Divining the Road" to lodge his own feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled Ch'ü Yüan's Divining and wrote Divining the Road to pour out his heart.

sentences.zh: 及秀廢，與諸儒修定五禮，授旅騎尉。

translations.literal: When Hsiu was deposed, together with the various Confucians he revised and fixed the Five Rites and was made Traveling Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Hsiu fell, he helped fix the Five Rites and was made Traveling Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書牛弘建議以為《禮》：諸侯絕傍期，大夫降一等。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Niu Hung proposed, citing the Rites: "Feudal lords cut off collateral mourning at the second degree; great officers reduce one degree."
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hung of Personnel proposed, citing the Rites: "Feudal lords end collateral mourning at the second degree; great officers reduce one degree."

sentences.zh: 今之上柱國雖不同古諸侯，比大夫可也，官在第二品，宜降傍親一等。

translations.literal: Today's Upper Pillar of State, though not the same as feudal lords of old, may be compared to great officers; his office is of the second rank, and collateral kin should be reduced one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Upper Pillar of State is not an ancient feudal lord, yet may be compared to a great officer; at second rank, collateral kin should mourn one degree less.

sentences.zh: 議者多以為然。

translations.literal: Most of those in the deliberation thought it correct.
translations.idiomatic: Most debaters agreed.

sentences.zh: 炫駁之曰：「古之仕者，宗一人而已，庶子不得進，由是先王重嫡。

translations.literal: Xuan refuted it, saying: "In antiquity those who took office honored but one lineage head; secondary sons could not advance—hence the former kings valued the primary heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan objected, saying: "In olden days office went to a single lineage head alone; younger sons did not rise—therefore the former kings held the primary line dear.

sentences.zh: 其宗子有分祿之義，族人與宗子雖疏遠，猶服衰三月，良由受其恩也。

translations.literal: The lineage head had the duty of distributing stipends; clansmen, though distant from the lineage head, still wore three months' mourning—truly because they received his bounty.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the line bore the obligation to share emoluments; kin, however far from him, still mourned three months in sackcloth—because they had tasted his grace.

sentences.zh: 令之仕者，位以才升，不限嫡庶，與古既異，何降之有。

translations.literal: Today's officeholders rise by talent, not limited to primary or secondary sons; already different from antiquity—what lowering would there be?
translations.idiomatic: Men now take rank by ability, not by whether they are primary or secondary sons; the age has parted from the ancients—why impose a lowering at all?

sentences.zh: 令之貴者，多忽近親，若或降之，人道之疏，自此始矣。

translations.literal: Today's nobles mostly neglect near kin; if one were to lower them, the thinning of human ties would begin from this.
translations.idiomatic: The great of today often slight close kin; should one demote them in mourning, the fraying of human bonds would start here.

sentences.zh: 」遂寢其事。

translations.literal: " Thus the matter was laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: " And so the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 開皇二十年，廢國子、四門及州縣學，唯置太學，博士二人，學生七十二人。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of K'ai-huang, the Directorate of Education, the Four Gates School, and the prefecture and county schools were abolished; only the Imperial University was kept, with two erudites and seventy-two students.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of K'ai-huang the Directorate of Education, the Four Gates, and all prefectural and county schools were shut; only the Imperial University remained, with two erudites and seventy-two students.

sentences.zh: 炫上表言學校不宜廢，情理甚切，帝不納。

translations.literal: Xuan memorialized that schools ought not be abolished; his reasoning was very urgent, but the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan submitted a memorial arguing that schools must not be abolished—his plea was urgent and heartfelt—and the emperor would not heed it.

sentences.zh: 時國家殷盛，皆以遼東為意。

translations.literal: At the time the state was prosperous and flourishing; all minds were set on Liaotung.
translations.idiomatic: The realm then stood full and strong; every mind turned toward Liaotung.

sentences.zh: 炫以為遼東不可伐，作《撫夷論》以諷焉。

translations.literal: Xuan held that Liaotung could not be attacked and composed the "Treatise on Pacifying the Barbarians" to admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan believed Liaotung could not be conquered and wrote the "Treatise on Pacifying the Yi" as a subtle warning.

sentences.zh: 當時莫有悟者。

translations.literal: At the time none understood.
translations.idiomatic: None at the time took his meaning.

sentences.zh: 及大業之季，三征不克，炫言方驗。

translations.literal: By the end of the Ta-yeh era, three campaigns had failed; only then was Xuan's word proved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ta-yeh years waned and three expeditions had failed, Xuan's warning at last stood vindicated.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，牛弘引炫修律令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Niu Hung had Xuan assist in revising statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang came to the throne, Niu Hung brought Xuan in to help revise the laws.

sentences.zh: 始文帝時，以刀筆吏類多小人，年久長奸，勢使然也；

translations.literal: In Emperor Wen's time, because clerks who wielded the brush were mostly petty men who grew wicked with long years—such was the force of circumstance;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen it was held that brush-wielding clerks were mostly small men who, the longer they served, the more they turned treacherous—such was the drift of the times;

sentences.zh: 又以風俗陵遲，婦人無節。

translations.literal: and because customs were in decline and women lacked restraint,
translations.idiomatic: and because custom had sunk and women lacked restraint,

sentences.zh: 於是立格：州縣佐吏，三年而代之；

translations.literal: thereupon rules were set: prefectural and county assistants were to be replaced every three years;
translations.idiomatic: rules were laid down: prefectural and county assistants must rotate every three years;

sentences.zh: 九品妻，無得再醮。

translations.literal: wives of the nine ranks might not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: and wives of officials of the nine ranks might not marry again.

sentences.zh: 炫著論以為不可，弘竟從之。

translations.literal: Xuan wrote a treatise holding this inadmissible, but Hung went along with it anyway.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wrote a treatise arguing this would not do, yet Hung followed the policy all the same.

sentences.zh: 諸郡置學官及流外給稟，皆發於炫。

translations.literal: The establishment of school officers in all commanderies and the granting of grain to those outside the regular rolls—all issued from Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The posting of school officers in every commandery and stipends for men outside the regular rolls—all these measures came from Xuan.

sentences.zh: 弘嘗問炫：「案《周禮》，士多而府史少，今令史百倍于前，判官減則不濟。

translations.literal: Hung once asked Xuan: "According to the Rites of Chou, scholars were many and repository clerks few; today the clerks are a hundredfold what they were, yet if reviewing officers are reduced the work will not get done.
translations.idiomatic: Hung once asked Xuan: "The Rites of Chou show many scholars and few repository clerks; today clerks outnumber the old count a hundredfold, yet cut the reviewing officers and nothing gets finished.

sentences.zh: 其故何也？

translations.literal: What is the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?"

sentences.zh: 」炫曰：「古人委任責成，歲終考其殿最，案不重校，文不繁悉，府史之任，掌要目而已。

translations.literal: " Xuan said: "The ancients entrusted tasks and held men responsible; at year's end they examined achievement and failure. Cases were not double-checked, documents were not elaborate; the clerk's charge was merely to keep the main headings.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan said: "The ancients delegated and demanded results; at year's end they graded achievement. Dockets were not re-checked, papers were not piled high—the clerk's task was only to hold the main headings.

sentences.zh: 今之文簿，恆慮勘覆鍛煉，若其不密，萬里追證百年舊案。

translations.literal: Today's documents and ledgers always fear review, re-examination, and forced confession; if they are not airtight, cases a hundred years old are pursued for proof a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Today's ledgers live in fear of audit, re-review, and forced confession; leave a gap and a hundred-year-old case is chased for proof a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 故諺云：'老吏抱案死。

translations.literal: Hence the proverb says: 'An old clerk dies embracing his files.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: 'The old clerk dies hugging his dossiers.

sentences.zh: '今古不同，若此之相懸也。

translations.literal: ' Antiquity and the present differ by a gulf like this.
translations.idiomatic: ' Past and present stand thus far apart.

sentences.zh: 事煩政弊，職此之由。

translations.literal: Affairs are vexed and government is harmed—here lies the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Business grows tangled and government sickens—this is the root of it.

sentences.zh: 」弘又問：「魏、齊之時，令史從容而已，今則不遑寧舍。

translations.literal: " Hung asked again: "In Wei and Ch'i times clerks were at ease; today they have no leisure even to rest.
translations.idiomatic: " Hung asked again: "Under Wei and Ch'i the clerks were unhurried; today they cannot spare a moment's rest.

sentences.zh: 其事何由？

translations.literal: What is the reason for this?"
translations.idiomatic: What accounts for it?"

sentences.zh: 」炫曰：「齊氏立州，不過數十；

translations.literal: " Xuan said: "The Ch'i house established prefectures—no more than several tens;
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan said: "When the Ch'i house set up prefectures there were no more than several tens;

sentences.zh: 三府行台，遞相統領，文書行下，不過十條。

translations.literal: the three offices and traveling secretariats supervised one another in turn; documents sent down ran to no more than ten items.
translations.idiomatic: the three ministries and traveling secretariats ruled one another in turn; papers sent down rarely exceeded ten items.

sentences.zh: 今州三百。

translations.literal: Today there are three hundred prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Today there are three hundred prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其繁一也。

translations.literal: This is the first source of congestion.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first burden.

sentences.zh: 往者，州唯置綱紀，郡置守、丞，縣唯令而已，其所具僚，則長官自辟，受詔赴任，每州不過數十。

translations.literal: Formerly a prefecture had only a chief administrator; a commandery had a prefect and assistant; a county had only a magistrate—the staff they assembled the chief appointed himself. Receiving the edict they went to their posts; each prefecture had no more than several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a prefecture kept only a chief coordinator; a commandery had prefect and assistant; a county had only a magistrate—staff were recruited by the chief himself. With the edict they went to post; each prefecture had fewer than several tens.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，大小之官，悉由吏部，纖介之跡，皆屬考功。

translations.literal: Today it is not so: great and small offices all come from the Ministry of Personnel; the slightest trace belongs to the Office of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is otherwise: every office great or small comes from the Ministry of Personnel; the smallest mark falls under the Office of Merit.

sentences.zh: 其繁二也。

translations.literal: This is the second source of congestion.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second burden.

sentences.zh: 省官不如省事，省事不如清心，官事不省而望從容，其可得乎！

translations.literal: To reduce offices is not as good as reducing business; to reduce business is not as good as clearing the heart. With official business unreduced yet hoping for ease—how can it be obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: Cutting posts is not equal to cutting work; cutting work is not equal to clearing the mind. Leave the work uncut and hope for ease—can that be had!"

sentences.zh: 」弘甚善其言而不能用。

translations.literal: " Hung greatly approved his words but could not apply them.
translations.idiomatic: " Hung admired his words deeply but could not put them into practice.

sentences.zh: 納言楊達舉炫博學有文章，射策高第，除太學博士。

translations.literal: The Counselor Yang Ta recommended Xuan as erudite and accomplished in letters; in the archery-and-writing examination he took a high grade and was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Counselor Yang Ta recommended Xuan for broad learning and literary skill; he placed high in the written examination and was made Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以品卑去任。

translations.literal: After more than a year, because his rank was low he left the post.
translations.idiomatic: After a year and more he left office, his rank being too low.

sentences.zh: 還至長平，奉敕追詣行在所。

translations.literal: Returning to Ch'ang-p'ing, he received an edict summoning him to the emperor's traveling residence.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back to Ch'ang-p'ing he was summoned by edict to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 或言其無行，帝遂罷之。

translations.literal: Some said he lacked conduct, and the emperor thereupon dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone spoke of his want of conduct, and the emperor set the appointment aside.

sentences.zh: 歸於河間。

translations.literal: He returned to Ho-chien.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to Ho-chien.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊峰起，穀食踴貴，經籍道息，教授不行。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose everywhere, grain soared in price, the way of the classics fell silent, and teaching ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed; grain leaped in price; the classics went untaught and instruction ceased.

sentences.zh: 炫與妻子，相去百里，聲聞斷絕，鬱鬱不得志，乃自為贊曰：

translations.literal: Xuan and his wife and children were a hundred li apart; word between them was cut off. Depressed and unfulfilled, he composed a self-eulogy, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was a hundred li from wife and children; no word passed between them. Sick at heart and thwarted, he wrote a self-eulogy, saying:

sentences.zh: 通人司馬相如、揚子雲、馬季長、鄭康成等皆自敘徽美，傳芳來葉。

translations.literal: Men of penetration—Ssu-ma Hsiang-ju, Yang Tzu-yün, Ma Chi-ch'ang, Cheng Hsüan, and others—all narrated their own fine qualities, leaving fragrance for later leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Men of penetration—Ssu-ma Hsiang-ju, Yang Tzu-yün, Ma Chi-ch'ang, Cheng Hsüan—each told his own worth and left fragrance for generations after.

sentences.zh: 余豈敢仰均先進，貽笑後昆？

translations.literal: How dare I look up to match the advanced and bring laughter on later generations?
translations.idiomatic: How dare I measure myself against those forebears and become a jest to those who come after?

sentences.zh: 徒以日迫桑榆，大命將近，故友飄零，門徒雨散，溘死朝露，魂埋朔野。

translations.literal: I only face the mulberry at sunset; the great mandate draws near. Old friends drift away; disciples scatter like rain. I shall die like morning dew; my soul will be buried in the northern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Only because the mulberry sun sinks and the great mandate nears—old friends scatter, disciples fly apart like rain—I shall die like morning dew and my soul lie in the northern wilds.

sentences.zh: 親故莫照其心，後人不見其跡。

translations.literal: Kin and friends do not illumine my heart; those who come after will not see my tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and friends do not light my heart; posterity will not see my trail.

sentences.zh: 殆及余喘，薄言胸臆，貽及行邁，傳之州裏，使夫將來俊哲，知餘鄙志耳。

translations.literal: While my breath yet lingers, let me speak briefly from the breast, reach to the road ahead, and pass it through the district, so that future brilliant men may know my humble intent.
translations.idiomatic: While breath yet remains, let me speak plainly from the breast and send it down the road through the district, that future wise men may know my humble mind.

sentences.zh: 餘從綰發以來，迄于白首，嬰孩為慈親所恕，捶撻未嘗加；

translations.literal: From the tying of my hair until white-haired age, as an infant I was indulged by a loving parent—never was the rod applied;
translations.idiomatic: From the tying of my hair to white old age: as a child I was spared by a loving parent—the rod never fell;

sentences.zh: 從學為明師所矜，榎楚弗之及。

translations.literal: in study I was prized by enlightened teachers—the mulberry switch never reached me.
translations.idiomatic: in study I was cherished by enlightened teachers—the mulberry switch never touched me.

sentences.zh: 暨乎敦敘邦族，交結等夷，重物輕身，先人後己。

translations.literal: When it came to ordering kin and befriending equals, I valued things lightly and my person heavily, putting others before myself.
translations.idiomatic: When I ordered kin and made friends among peers, I prized goods lightly and the self heavily, and put others before myself.

sentences.zh: 昔在幼弱，樂參長者；

translations.literal: Formerly in youth and weakness I delighted in joining my elders;
translations.idiomatic: In youth I delighted to keep company with elders;

sentences.zh: 爰及耆艾，數接後生。

translations.literal: reaching gray age I often received the young.
translations.idiomatic: in gray age I often welcomed the young.

sentences.zh: 學則服而不厭，誨則勞而不倦。

translations.literal: In learning I was never weary of being taught; in teaching I toiled yet never tired.
translations.idiomatic: In learning I never tired of being taught; in teaching I labored and did not weary.

sentences.zh: 幽情寡適，心事多違。

translations.literal: Secluded feeling found little fit; affairs of the heart mostly went against me.
translations.idiomatic: In solitude I found little ease; what the heart wished mostly went awry.

sentences.zh: 內省生平，顧循終始，其大幸有四，深恨有一。

translations.literal: Looking within on my life and tracing it from beginning to end, I have four great blessings and one deep regret.
translations.idiomatic: Looking inward over my life from start to finish, I count four great blessings and one deep regret.

sentences.zh: 性本愚蔽，家業貧窶，為父兄所饒，廁縉紳之末。

translations.literal: My nature was originally dull and obscured; my family estate was poor. Yet my father and elder brothers indulged me, and I stood at the hem of the girdled ranks.
translations.idiomatic: By nature I was dull and my house poor; yet father and brothers indulged me and I stood among the girdled ranks.

sentences.zh: 遂得博覽典誥，窺涉今古，小善著於丘園，虛名聞于邦國。

translations.literal: Thus I could roam the canonical texts and glimpse present and past; small good was noted in my garden, empty fame heard in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I ranged the classics and touched present and past; small merit showed in my garden, hollow fame sounded in the realm.

sentences.zh: 其幸一也。

translations.literal: This was the first blessing.
translations.idiomatic: That was the first blessing.

sentences.zh: 隱顯人間，沈浮世俗，數忝徒勞之職，久執城旦之書。

translations.literal: Hidden and manifest among men, sinking and floating in the world, I repeatedly held thankless posts and long kept the "city-dawn" documents.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden and shown among men, sunk and floated in the world, I often held thankless posts and long kept the penal registers.

sentences.zh: 名不掛于白簡，事不染於丹筆。

translations.literal: My name did not hang on the white bamboo; my affairs were not stained by the vermilion brush.
translations.idiomatic: My name never hung on the impeachment slips; my deeds were never marked by the censor's brush.

sentences.zh: 立身立行，慚恧實多，啟手啟足，庶幾可免。

translations.literal: In establishing person and conduct I have much to blush for, yet in hand and foot I may almost escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: In person and conduct I have much to blush for, yet in hand and foot I may nearly escape reproach.

sentences.zh: 其幸二也。

translations.literal: This was the second blessing.
translations.idiomatic: That was the second blessing.

sentences.zh: 以此庸虛，屢動宸眷；

translations.literal: With this mediocrity and emptiness I repeatedly moved the sovereign's regard;
translations.idiomatic: With this mediocrity I yet stirred the Son of Heaven's favor again and again;

sentences.zh: 以此卑賤，每升天府。

translations.literal: with this baseness and low rank I repeatedly ascended the heavenly offices.
translations.idiomatic: with this low rank I yet climbed again and again to the halls of state.

sentences.zh: 齊鑣驥騄，比翼鵷鴻，整槹素于鳳池，記言動於麟閣。

translations.literal: I matched swift horses and fine steeds, paired wings with yuan and wild swans, set the plain staff in the Phoenix Pool, and recorded words and deeds in the Unicorn Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: I ran beside swift horses and fine steeds, wing to wing with yuan and wild swans, set the plain staff in the Phoenix Pool, and recorded words and deeds in the Unicorn Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 參謁宰輔，造請群公，厚禮殊恩，增榮改價。

translations.literal: I paid calls on chief ministers and visited the host of nobles; thick gifts and special favor raised my honor and changed my price.
translations.idiomatic: I called on chief ministers and sought out the great; rich gifts and special grace raised my honor and changed my worth.

sentences.zh: 其幸三也。

translations.literal: This was the third blessing.
translations.idiomatic: That was the third blessing.

sentences.zh: 晝漏方盡，大耋已嗟，退反初服，歸骸故里。

translations.literal: The day clepsydra was nearly spent; great old age already sighed. I withdrew to my first garments and returned my bones to my native place.
translations.idiomatic: The day-water was nearly spent; great age already lamented. I put off office and returned my bones to my native soil.

sentences.zh: 玩文史以怡神，閱魚鳥以散慮。

translations.literal: I delighted in letters and histories to cheer the spirit and watched fish and birds to scatter cares.
translations.idiomatic: I took joy in letters and histories to refresh the spirit and watched fish and birds to scatter care.

sentences.zh: 觀省野物，登臨園沼，緩步代車，無事為貴。

translations.literal: I observed the things of the wilds and climbed gardens and ponds; slow steps replaced the carriage—having nothing to do was precious.
translations.idiomatic: I looked on wild things, climbed gardens and ponds, walked where others rode—having nothing to do was the treasure.

sentences.zh: 其幸四也。

translations.literal: This was the fourth blessing.
translations.idiomatic: That was the fourth blessing.

sentences.zh: 仰休明之盛世，慨道教之陵遲，蹈先儒之逸軌，傷群言之蕪穢。

translations.literal: Looking up at a brilliant flourishing age, I grieved that the Way of teaching was in decline; I trod the abandoned tracks of former Confucians and mourned the rank growth among the many sayings.
translations.idiomatic: I looked up at a radiant age and grieved that the teaching Way had sunk; I followed the lost tracks of former ru and mourned the weeds choking the many texts.

sentences.zh: 馳騁墳典，厘改僻謬，修撰始畢，事業適成。

translations.literal: I galloped through the classics and tombs, corrected errors and strangeness; compilation was just finished and the work complete.
translations.idiomatic: I ranged the classics and tombs, corrected errors and strangeness; the writing was finished and the work stood complete.

sentences.zh: 天違人願，途不我與，世路未夷，學校盡廢，道不備於當時，業不傳於身後。

translations.literal: Heaven opposed human wish; the road would not walk with me. The world's path was not level; schools were wholly abolished. The Way was not complete in the age; the work would not pass to those after.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven crossed human wish; the road would not keep me company. The world was not at peace; schools were abolished to the last. The Way was not whole in the time; the work would not live after my body.

sentences.zh: 銜恨泉壤，實在茲乎！

translations.literal: To harbor regret in the springs below—truly it lies here!
translations.idiomatic: To carry regret into the yellow springs—here indeed it lies!

sentences.zh: 其深恨一也。

translations.literal: This was the one deep regret.
translations.idiomatic: That was the one deep regret.

sentences.zh: 時在郡城，糧餉斷絕。

translations.literal: At the time he was in the commandery city; grain and provisions were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He was then in the commandery seat; grain and supplies ran out.

sentences.zh: 其門人多隨賊盜。

translations.literal: Most of his disciples followed the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his disciples went over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 哀炫窮乏，詣城下索炫，郡官乃出炫與之。

translations.literal: Ai, pitying Xuan's destitution, came below the wall to demand Xuan; the commandery officials thereupon handed Xuan over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ai, moved by Xuan's want, came beneath the wall to demand him; the commandery officials then surrendered Xuan to him.

sentences.zh: 炫為賊所將，過下城堡。

translations.literal: Xuan was led by the bandits and passed the lower castle.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was marched off by the rebels and passed the lower fort.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊為官軍所破，炫饑餓無所依，復投縣官。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits were broken by government troops; Xuan, hungry and with nowhere to rely, again sought the county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels were broken by government troops; hungry and with nowhere to turn, Xuan again sought the county office.

sentences.zh: 縣官意炫與賊相知，恐為後變，遂閉門不納。

translations.literal: The county officials thought Xuan was on familiar terms with the bandits and feared later trouble, so they closed the gate and would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate thought Xuan knew the rebels and feared future trouble; he shut the gate and would not take him in.

sentences.zh: 時夜冰寒，因此凍餒而死。

translations.literal: The night was icy cold; thus he died of cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The night was bitter cold; there he died of cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 其後門人諡曰宣德先生。

translations.literal: Afterward his disciples gave him the posthumous title Master Hsüan-te.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward his disciples gave him the posthumous style Master Hsüan-te.

sentences.zh: 炫性躁競，頗好俳諧，多自矜伐，好輕侮當世，為執政所醜，由是宦途不遂。

translations.literal: Xuan's nature was impatient and contentious; he rather liked jest and banter, often praised himself, and liked to slight the men of the age. The wielders of power detested him, and thus his official path did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was hasty and contentious, fond of jest and banter, given to self-praise and to slighting the men of his day; those in power loathed him, and his road to office never opened.

sentences.zh: 著《論語述議》十卷、《春秋攻昧》十卷、《五經正名》十二卷、《孝經述議》五卷、《春秋述議》四十卷、《尚書述議》二十卷、《毛詩述議》四十卷，注《詩序》一卷、《算術》一卷，並所著文集，並行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote the Expository Discourse on the Analects in ten scrolls, Attack on Obscurity in the Spring and Autumn in ten scrolls, Correct Names of the Five Classics in twelve scrolls, Expository Discourse on the Classic of Filial Piety in five scrolls, Expository Discourse on the Spring and Autumn in forty scrolls, Expository Discourse on the Documents in twenty scrolls, Expository Discourse on the Mao Odes in forty scrolls; he annotated the Preface to the Odes in one scroll and Arithmetic in one scroll, together with his collected writings—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Expository Discourse on the Analects (10 juan), Attack on Obscurity in the Spring and Autumn (10 juan), Correct Names of the Five Classics (12 juan), Expository Discourse on the Filial Classic (5 juan), on the Spring and Autumn (40 juan), on the Documents (20 juan), on the Mao Odes (40 juan); he annotated the Preface to the Odes and wrote Arithmetic (1 juan each), with his collected writings—all in circulation.

sentences.zh: 時儒學之士，又有褚暉、顧彪、魯世達、張沖、王孝籍並知名。

translations.literal: Among Confucian scholars of the time there were also Chu Hui, Ku Piao, Lu Shih-ta, Chang Chong, and Wang Hsiao-chi—all famed.
translations.idiomatic: Among the ru of the time Chu Hui, Ku Piao, Lu Shih-ta, Chang Chong, and Wang Hsiao-chi were also well known.

sentences.zh: 褚暉，字高明，吳郡人。

translations.literal: Chu Hui, style Kao-ming, was a man of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Hui, style Kao-ming, came from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 以《三禮》學稱於江南。

translations.literal: He was famed south of the Yangtze for learning in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze he was famed for mastery of the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，徵天下儒術之士，悉集內史省，相次講論。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang's time all Confucian scholars under heaven were summoned and gathered in the Inner Secretariat, lecturing in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang the empire's Confucians were summoned to the Inner Secretariat and lectured in turn.

sentences.zh: 暉辯博，無能屈者，由是擢為太學博士。

translations.literal: Hui was broad in debate and none could overcome him; thereby he was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Hui debated with breadth and none could best him; he was raised to Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 撰疏一百卷。

translations.literal: He wrote commentaries in a hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He composed commentaries in a hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 顧彪，字仲文，余杭人。

translations.literal: Ku Piao, style Chung-wen, was a man of Yü-hang.
translations.idiomatic: Ku Piao, style Chung-wen, was from Yü-hang.

sentences.zh: 明《尚書》、《春秋》。

translations.literal: He was accomplished in the Documents and the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the Documents and the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，為秘書學士。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang's time he was a Secretary Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he served as Secretary Scholar.

sentences.zh: 撰《古文尚書義疏》二十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote the Expository Commentary on the Ancient Text Documents in twenty scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Expository Commentary on the Ancient Text Documents in twenty scrolls, which circulated.

sentences.zh: 魯世達，余杭人。

translations.literal: Lu Shih-ta was a man of Yü-hang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shih-ta was from Yü-hang.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，為國子助教。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang's time he was an Assistant Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he was Assistant Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 撰《毛詩章句義疏》四十二卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote the Expository Commentary on the Mao Odes by Chapter and Phrase in forty-two scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Expository Commentary on the Mao Odes by Chapter and Phrase in forty-two scrolls, which circulated.

sentences.zh: 張沖，字叔玄，吳郡人。

translations.literal: Chang Chong, style Shu-hsüan, was a man of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Chong, style Shu-hsüan, was from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，為左中郎將，非其好也。

translations.literal: He served Ch'en as Left Gentlemen-of-the-Guard—it was not his liking.
translations.idiomatic: In Ch'en he served as Left Gentlemen-of-the-Guard—a post he did not love.

sentences.zh: 乃覃思經典，撰《春秋義略》，異于杜氏七十餘事，《喪服義》三卷、《孝經義》三卷、《論語義》十卷、《前漢音義》十二卷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pondered deeply the classics and wrote the Essentials of Meaning in the Spring and Autumn, differing from the Tu family in more than seventy matters, Mourning Dress Meaning in three scrolls, Filial Classic Meaning in three scrolls, Analects Meaning in ten scrolls, and Sounds and Meaning of the Former Han in twelve scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to the classics in deep study and wrote the Essentials of Meaning in the Spring and Autumn, differing from the Tu tradition in more than seventy points, plus Mourning Dress Meaning (3 juan), Filial Classic Meaning (3 juan), Analects Meaning (10 juan), and Sounds and Meaning of the Former Han (12 juan).

sentences.zh: 官至漢王侍讀。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Reader to the Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Reader to the Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 王孝籍，平原人。

translations.literal: Wang Hsiao-chi was a man of P'ing-yüan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hsiao-chi was from P'ing-yüan.

sentences.zh: 少好學，博覽群言，遍習《五經》，頗有文翰。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, roamed widely among the many sayings, studied all the Five Classics throughout, and had considerable literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved learning, ranged widely among texts, mastered all the Five Classics, and wrote with some skill.

sentences.zh: 與河間劉炫，同志友善。

translations.literal: With Liu Xuan of Ho-chien he shared the same aims and were close friends.
translations.idiomatic: He shared aims and close friendship with Liu Xuan of Ho-chien.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，召入秘書，助王劭修國史。

translations.literal: In the K'ai-huang era he was summoned to the Secretariat to assist Wang Shao in revising the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In K'ai-huang he was called to the Secretariat to help Wang Shao revise the national history.

sentences.zh: 劭不之禮。

translations.literal: Shao did not treat him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Shao did not honor him.

sentences.zh: 在省多年，不免輸稅，鬱鬱不得志，奏記于吏部尚書牛弘曰：

translations.literal: After many years in the Secretariat he still could not escape paying taxes. Depressed and unfulfilled, he submitted a letter to the Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, Niu Hung, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Years in the Secretariat yet he still paid taxes like any commoner. Sick at heart, he wrote to Minister of Personnel Niu Hung, saying:

sentences.zh: 竊以毒螫絪膚，則申旦不寐；

translations.literal: I venture to think: when poison stings and binds the skin, one cannot sleep from mid-night to dawn;
translations.idiomatic: I venture: when poison stings the skin one cannot sleep from midnight to dawn;

sentences.zh: 饑寒切體，亦卒歲無聊。

translations.literal: when hunger and cold cut the body, one is likewise joyless the whole year.
translations.idiomatic: when hunger and cold cut the flesh, the whole year knows no ease.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 痛苦難以安，貧窮易為戚。

translations.literal: Pain is hard to rest in; poverty easily becomes sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Pain will not let one rest; poverty easily turns to grief.

sentences.zh: 況懷抱之內，冰火鑠脂膏，腠理之間，風霜侵骨髓。

translations.literal: Moreover, within the bosom ice and fire melt the fat; between the pores wind and frost invade the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Within the breast ice and fire melt the fat; in the pores wind and frost gnaw the marrow.

sentences.zh: 安可齰舌緘脣，吞聲飲氣，惡呻吟之響，忍酸辛之酷哉！

translations.literal: How can one bite the tongue and seal the lips, swallow the voice and drink the breath, hate the sound of groaning, and endure the bitterness of acid suffering!
translations.idiomatic: How can one bite the tongue, seal the lips, swallow voice and breath, hate the sound of groaning, and endure such bitter pain!

sentences.zh: 伏惟明尚書公，動哀矜之色，開寬裕之懷，咳唾足以活涸鱗，吹噓可用飛窮羽。

translations.literal: I bow before the enlightened Minister: move a countenance of compassion, open a breast of generosity—spittle and cough are enough to revive a dried fish; breath and puff can make a poor bird fly.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before the enlightened Minister: show a face of pity, open a heart of grace—a word from you revives the dried fish; your breath lifts the fallen bird.

sentences.zh: 芬椒蘭之氣，暖布帛之詞，許小人之請，聞大君之聽。

translations.literal: The fragrance of pepper and orchid, warm words like cloth and silk—grant the petty man's request and let the great lord hear.
translations.idiomatic: Let pepper and orchid scent your words; let cloth and silk warm them—grant this petty man's plea and let the great lord listen.

sentences.zh: 雖復山川綿遠，鬼神在茲，信而有征，言無不履。

translations.literal: Though mountains and rivers stretch far and ghosts stand here, what is believed has proof; no word fails of fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Though mountains and rivers lie far and ghosts attend, faith has signs; no word of yours fails to stand.

sentences.zh: 猶恐拯溺遲於援手，救跌緩於扶足，待越人之舟楫，求魯燕之雲梯，則必懸于喬樹之枝，沒於深泉之底。

translations.literal: I still fear that saving the drowned is slower than the helping hand, that rescuing the fallen is slower than the supporting foot—that waiting for the Yüeh man's boat and seeking the Lu and Yen cloud-ladder, one must hang from the tall tree's branch and sink to the deep spring's bottom.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that to save the drowning is slower than the hand that reaches, to lift the fallen slower than the foot that steadies—wait for the Yüeh man's boat and the Lu and Yen cloud-ladder, and one will hang from the high branch and sink to the deep spring.

sentences.zh: 夫以一介貧人，七年直省，課役不免，慶賞不沾。

translations.literal: For a single poor man to hold straight office in the Secretariat seven years, yet not escape corvée and tax and receive no reward or bounty—
translations.idiomatic: A single poor man, seven years straight service in the Secretariat, yet corvée and tax never lifted, reward and bounty never granted—

sentences.zh: 賣貢禹之田，供釋之之費；

translations.literal: he sells Kung Yü's fields to supply the expenses of Shih;
translations.idiomatic: he sells Kung Yü's fields to pay Shih's costs;

sentences.zh: 有弱子之累，乏強兄之產。

translations.literal: he has the burden of weak sons and lacks a strong elder brother's estate.
translations.idiomatic: he bears weak sons and lacks a strong brother's estate.

sentences.zh: 加以慈母在堂，光陰遲暮，寒暑違闕，關山超遠。

translations.literal: Moreover his loving mother is at home; her light and shade are late; cold and heat miss their seasons; mountains and passes stretch beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: His mother still lives; her years are late; he cannot tend cold and heat; mountains and passes lie far away.

sentences.zh: 齧臂為期，前途逾邈；

translations.literal: He bites his arm to set a date, yet the road ahead grows ever more distant;
translations.idiomatic: He bites his arm to fix a return, yet the road ahead only lengthens;

sentences.zh: 倚閭之望，朝夕傾對。

translations.literal: the leaning-on-the-hedge gaze morning and evening turns in longing.
translations.idiomatic: his mother leans on the hedge and waits, morning and evening, straining toward him.

sentences.zh: 謝相如之病，無官可以免；

translations.literal: Hsiang-ju's illness of old had no office by which to be excused;
translations.idiomatic: Ssu-ma Hsiang-ju's old sickness had no office by which to win release;

sentences.zh: 發梅福之狂，非仙所能避。

translations.literal: Mei Fu's madness could not be avoided even by immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Fu's madness not even an immortal could ward off.

sentences.zh: 愁疾甚乎厲鬼，人生異夫金石。

translations.literal: Sorrow and illness exceed the evil ghost; human life differs from metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Grief and sickness outdo the evil ghost; human life is not metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 營魂且散，恐筮予無徵；

translations.literal: The camp-soul is about to scatter; I fear the divination for me has no sign;
translations.idiomatic: The soul is about to scatter; I fear the oracle for me shows no sign;

sentences.zh: 齎恨入冥，則虛緣恩顧。

translations.literal: carry regret into the dark and the favor of your regard will have been in vain.
translations.idiomatic: carry regret into the dark and your gracious regard will have been empty.

sentences.zh: 此乃王稽所以致言，應侯為之不樂也。

translations.literal: This is why Wang Chi spoke out and why the Marquis of Ying was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Wang Chi spoke up and the Marquis of Ying grew unhappy.

sentences.zh: 潛鬢髮之內，居眉睫之間，子野未曾聞，離硃所未見。

translations.literal: It lies hidden within the temples of the hair and dwells between the eyebrows; Tzu-yeh never heard of it; Li Chu never saw it.
translations.idiomatic: It hides in the temples of the hair and lives between the eyebrows—Tzu-yeh never heard of it, Li Chu never saw it.

sentences.zh: 久淪東觀，留滯南史，終無薦引，永同埋殯。

translations.literal: Long sunk in the Eastern Pavilion, detained in the Southern History—never a recommendation, forever like a buried coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Long sunk in the Eastern Pavilion, stuck on the Southern History—never recommended, forever like a coffin in the earth.

sentences.zh: 三世不移，雖由寂寞；

translations.literal: Three generations without transfer—though that comes from obscurity;
translations.idiomatic: Three generations without promotion—though that comes from obscurity;

sentences.zh: 十年不調，實乏知己。

translations.literal: ten years without appointment—truly I lack a knower.
translations.idiomatic: ten years without appointment—truly I lack one who knows me.

sentences.zh: 夫不世出者，聖明之君也；

translations.literal: He who does not appear once in an age is a sage and enlightened lord;
translations.idiomatic: The lord who appears once in an age is the sage ruler;

sentences.zh: 不萬一者，誠賢之臣也。

translations.literal: he who is not one in ten thousand is a truly worthy minister.
translations.idiomatic: the minister who is one in ten thousand is the truly worthy man.

sentences.zh: 以夫不世出而逢不萬一，小人所以為明尚書幸也。

translations.literal: That one not of the age should meet one not in ten thousand—this petty man therefore counts the enlightened Minister fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: That this unlucky age should meet this one-in-ten-thousand minister—this petty man therefore calls the enlightened Minister blessed.

sentences.zh: 坐人物之源，運銓衡之柄，反被狐白，不好緇衣，此小人為明尚書不取也。

translations.literal: Sitting at the source of men and things, wielding the handle of the balance, yet wrapping fox-fur and not loving black robes—this the petty man counts against the enlightened Minister.
translations.idiomatic: You sit at the spring of men and things and hold the balance—yet you wrap yourself in fox fur and do not love the black robe; this petty man counts against you.

sentences.zh: 昔荊玉未剖，刖卞和之足；

translations.literal: Formerly before the Ching jade was split open, Pien Ho's feet were cut off;
translations.idiomatic: Once, before the Ching jade was opened, Pien Ho's feet were severed;

sentences.zh: 百里未用，碎禽息之首。

translations.literal: before Po-li was employed, Ch'in Wu's head was smashed.
translations.idiomatic: before Po-li was used, Ch'in Wu's head was broken.

sentences.zh: 居得言之地，有能用之資，憎耳目之明，無首足之戚，憚而不為，孰知其解！

translations.literal: Occupying a place where words may be spoken, possessing talent that can be employed, yet hating the brightness of eye and ear and having no worry for head and foot—dreading yet not acting, who knows the reason!
translations.idiomatic: You stand where speech is heard and have power to employ talent—yet you hate clear sight and sound and feel no fear for head or foot; you shrink and do not act—who understands why!

sentences.zh: 夫官或不稱其能，士或未申其屈，一夫竊議，語流天下，勞不見圖，安能無望！

translations.literal: When office does not match ability or a scholar does not declare his wrong, one man whispers and the words flow under heaven; labor unseen in the plan—how can there be no hope!
translations.idiomatic: When office does not fit ability or a scholar cannot voice his wrong, one man whispers and the tale runs under heaven; labor unseen in the plan—how can one not still hope!

sentences.zh: 倘病未及死，狂還克念，汗窮愁之簡，屬離憂之詞。

translations.literal: If illness has not yet reached death and madness can yet recall thought, I will wet the bamboo of utter destitution and entrust words of parting sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: If sickness has not yet killed me and madness can still turn to thought, I will wet the slips of utter want and leave words of parting grief.

sentences.zh: 托志于前修，通心於來哲，使千載之下，哀其不遇，追咎執事，有玷清塵。

translations.literal: I entrust my aim to the former cultivated and open my heart to sages to come, so that a thousand years below they may pity my ill fortune, trace blame to the executor, and stain the clear dust.
translations.idiomatic: I set my aim with the ancients and my heart with sages yet unborn, that a thousand years hence they may pity my ill lot, lay blame on the officer, and stain his clear name.

sentences.zh: 則不肖之軀，死生為累，小人之罪，方且未刊。

translations.literal: Then this unworthy body, living and dying, becomes a burden; the petty man's fault is not yet expunged.
translations.idiomatic: Then this worthless body, in life and death, will be your burden; this petty man's fault will not yet be wiped away.

sentences.zh: 願少加憐湣，留心無忽。

translations.literal: I beg a little pity and attention without neglect.
translations.idiomatic: I beg a little pity—do not forget me.

sentences.zh: 弘亦知其學業，而竟不得調。

translations.literal: Hung also knew his learning, yet in the end he could not secure an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Hung knew his learning too, yet never secured him a post.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，以教授為業，終於家。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his native district and took teaching as his occupation, dying at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went home and lived by teaching until he died in his house.

sentences.zh: 注《尚書》及《詩》，遭亂零落。

translations.literal: His commentaries on the Documents and the Odes were lost in the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: His commentaries on the Documents and the Odes were scattered in the chaos.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古語云：「容體不足觀，勇力不足恃，族姓不足道，先祖不足稱，然而顯聞四方，流聲後胤者，其惟學乎？

translations.literal: The discussion says: An old saying runs: "The body is not worth viewing, courage and strength not worth relying on, clan and surname not worth speaking of, forebears not worth praising—yet to be illustrious in the four quarters and leave a sound for later generations: is it not learning?"
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: An old saying runs: "Form is not worth looking at, strength not worth trusting, clan not worth naming, ancestors not worth praising—yet to shine in the four quarters and leave a name to posterity: is it not learning?"

sentences.zh: 」信哉斯言也！

translations.literal: " How true are these words!
translations.idiomatic: " How true that is!

sentences.zh: 梁越之徒，篤志不倦，自求諸己，遂能聞道下風，稱珍席上。

translations.literal: Men like Liang Yüeh and his kind, with steadfast aim never weary, seeking from themselves, were able to hear the Way below the wind and be called treasures at the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Liang Yüeh, steadfast and unwearied, seeking from within themselves, could hear the Way from afar and be called treasures at the high table.

sentences.zh: 或聚徒千百，或服冕乘軒，咸稽古之力也。

translations.literal: Some gathered disciples by the hundreds; some wore caps and rode carriages—all the power of investigating antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Some gathered hundreds of disciples; some wore caps and rode in carriages—all through the force of classical learning.

sentences.zh: 然遠惟漢、魏，碩學多清通；

translations.literal: Yet looking far to Han and Wei, great scholars were mostly clear and penetrating;
translations.idiomatic: Yet look far to Han and Wei: great scholars were mostly clear and penetrating;

sentences.zh: 逮乎近古，巨儒多鄙俗。

translations.literal: reaching near antiquity, great Confucians were mostly base and vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: come to recent times and great ru are mostly coarse and vulgar.

sentences.zh: 文武不墜，弘之在人，豈獨愚蔽於當今，而皆明哲於往昔？

translations.literal: That wen and wu do not fall depends on the man who extends them—are only the stupid and obscured of today so, while all of the past were wise and clear?
translations.idiomatic: That culture and arms do not fall depends on the man who spreads them—are only today's men dull while all the past were wise?

sentences.zh: 在乎用與不用，知與不知耳。

translations.literal: It lies in employing or not employing, knowing or not knowing.
translations.idiomatic: It lies in use or disuse, knowing or not knowing.

sentences.zh: 然曩之弼諧庶績，必舉德于鴻儒；

translations.literal: Yet formerly in harmonizing the many tasks, virtue was always raised from great Confucians;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in olden days, in harmonizing the many tasks, virtue was always drawn from great ru;

sentences.zh: 近代左右邦家，咸取士於刀筆。

translations.literal: in recent times those at the ruler's left and right in governing the state all took their men from the brush.
translations.idiomatic: in recent times those who stood at the ruler's side in governing the state all took men from the brush.

sentences.zh: 縱有學優入室，勤逾刺股，名高海內，擢第甲科，若命偶時來，未有望於青紫；

translations.literal: Even if learning was excellent enough to enter the inner room, diligence exceeded pricking the thigh, fame was high within the seas, and one was chosen in the first rank of the examination—if fate did not pair with the time, there was still no hope of purple and scarlet;
translations.idiomatic: Even if learning could enter the inner room, diligence outdid the thigh-pricker, fame filled the seas, and one topped the examination—if fate and hour did not align, there was still no hope of purple and scarlet;

sentences.zh: 或數將運舛，必見棄於草澤。

translations.literal: or if several times fortune turned adverse, one was sure to be cast off in the grass and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: or if fortune turned several times against one, one was sure to be abandoned in the wilds.

sentences.zh: 然則古之學者，祿在其中；

translations.literal: Thus the scholars of antiquity had their stipends within their learning;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the scholars of old had salary within their learning;

sentences.zh: 今之學者，困于貧賤。

translations.literal: the scholars of today are trapped in poverty and baseness.
translations.idiomatic: the scholars of today are trapped in want and low estate.

sentences.zh: 明達之人，志識之士，安肯滯于所習，以求貧賤者哉！

translations.literal: Clear-sighted men and men of will and knowledge—how would they linger in what they have mastered to seek poverty and baseness!
translations.idiomatic: Men of insight and firm purpose—how would they cling to what they have mastered only to seek poverty!

sentences.zh: 此所以儒罕通人，學多鄙俗者也。

translations.literal: This is why Confucians rarely produce penetrating men and learning is mostly base and vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: This is why ru rarely produce penetrating men and learning grows coarse and vulgar.

sentences.zh: 至若劉焯，德冠縉紳，數窮天象，既精且博，洞究幽微，鉤深致遠，源流不測。

translations.literal: As for Liu Chao, his virtue crowned the girdled ranks; in numbers he exhausted heavenly signs. Both refined and broad, he penetrated the subtle; hooking the deep he reached far—his source-stream cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: As for Liu Chao, virtue crowned the court; in number he exhausted the signs of heaven—refined and broad, probing the subtle, hooking the deep and reaching far, his source-stream none can sound.

sentences.zh: 數百年來，斯一人而已。

translations.literal: In several hundred years there has been only this one man.
translations.idiomatic: In several hundred years there has been only this one.

sentences.zh: 劉炫學實通儒，才堪成務，九流七略，無不該覽。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan's learning was truly that of a penetrating Confucian; his talent could accomplish tasks. Of the Nine Schools and Seven Summaries none was not covered in his reading.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan's learning was truly that of a penetrating ru; his talent could carry great affairs. Of the Nine Schools and Seven Summaries none escaped his reading.

sentences.zh: 雖探賾索隱，不逮於焯；

translations.literal: Though in probing the hidden and seeking the obscure he did not reach Chao;
translations.idiomatic: Though in probing the hidden and seeking the obscure he did not match Chao;

sentences.zh: 裁成義說，文雅過之。

translations.literal: in trimming and completing exegetical meaning he surpassed him in elegance.
translations.idiomatic: in shaping exegetical meaning and literary grace he surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 並時不我與，餒棄溝壑。

translations.literal: Both alike—the time did not walk with them; they starved and were cast into gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Both alike—the time would not keep them; they starved and were cast into ditches.

sentences.zh: 斯乃子夏所謂，「死生有命，富貴在天」。

translations.literal: This is what Tzu-hsia meant: "Life and death are by fate; wealth and honor are by Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: This is what Tzu-hsia meant: "Life and death are by fate; wealth and honor are by Heaven."

sentences.zh: 天之所與者聰明，所不與者貴仕，上聖且猶不免，焯、炫其如命何！

translations.literal: What Heaven gives is intelligence; what it does not give is noble office—even the highest sage could not escape this; what could Chao and Xuan do against fate!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gives intelligence; it does not give noble rank—even the highest sage could not escape it; what could Chao and Xuan do against fate!

sentences.zh: 孝籍徒離騷其文，尚何救也！

translations.literal: Hsiao-chi merely patterned the Li-sao in his writing—how could it save him!
translations.idiomatic: Hsiao-chi only patterned the Li-sao in his prose—what could that save!
